decisions.reason: Defines a vehicle wiring harness as supply, bus, signal or antenna cables installed by the vehicle manufacturer. The rear lamp is a lighting module, not a harness.

Defines immunity-related functions. Item (c)(i) names stop lamps and the rear position lamp as functions whose incorrect operation causes optical disturbance. The product performs rear position and stop functions, so this definition is relevant background. It creates no obligation.
Defines REESS as the rechargeable energy storage for electric propulsion. The rear lamp has no propulsion energy storage.

Paragraph 2.14 defines the coupling system for charging the REESS, which is an EV charging circuit. The product is a rear lamp module (position, stop, reversing lamps, outer lens, retro-reflector) with no charging circuit or REESS connection in the specification, so the definition does not apply to this product.
Paragraph 2.15 defines REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid, which concerns vehicle charging operation. The rear lamp specification contains no charging function or grid connection.
Paragraph 2.16 defines Mode 1 charging per IEC 61851-1. The rear lamp is a lighting and signalling module with no AC mains connection or charging function, so this definition does not apply.
Paragraph 2.17 defines Mode 2 charging per IEC 61851-1. The rear lamp specification describes no charging harness, EVSE, or pilot signalling, so the definition does not apply.
Paragraph 2.18 defines Mode 3 charging with EVSE communication. The rear lamp has no charging or communication interface in the specification, so this definition does not apply.
Paragraph 2.19 defines Mode 4 DC charging. The rear lamp specification has no DC charging function, so this definition does not apply.
Paragraph 2.20 defines signal/control ports (RS-232, USB, CAN, control pilot, etc.). The rear lamp specification lists no data or signal ports, so this definition does not apply.
Paragraph 2.21 defines wired network ports (CATV, LAN, xDSL, etc.). The rear lamp specification lists no network port, so this definition does not apply.

Paragraph 2.22 defines the asymmetric artificial network (AAN) test network. This is a test-equipment definition for vehicles in charging mode and has no link to the rear lamp's components or functions.

Paragraph 2.23 defines the DC charging artificial network inserted in the HV DC lead of a vehicle in charging mode. The rear lamp has no HV DC lead or charging function, so this definition does not apply.

Paragraph 2.24 defines the artificial mains network (AMN/LISN) used in EMC testing of vehicles in charging mode. The rear lamp has no power mains connection in charging mode, so this definition does not apply.
Paragraph 2.25 defines the Outdoor Test Site (OTS) for EMC radiated measurements. It is a test-site definition with no bearing on the rear lamp's design or function.

Paragraph 2.26 defines Automated Driving System (ADS). It is a definition, not an obligation, and the rear lamp spec describes a passive exterior lighting module with no driving-automation hardware or software.
Paragraph 2.27 defines Dynamic Driving Task (DDT), a definition with no obligation. The rear lamp spec has no driving-task functions.
Paragraph 2.28 defines ADS failure situations, a definition with no obligation. The rear lamp spec describes no ADS or vehicle-system failure function.
Paragraph 2.29 defines the residential electromagnetic environment by reference to IEC 61000-6-3. It is a definition only and does not apply to a rear lamp component.
Paragraph 2.30 defines the non-residential electromagnetic environment by reference to IEC 61000-6-4. It is a definition only and does not apply to a rear lamp component.
Paragraph 2.31 defines the Acoustic Vehicle Alerting System (AVAS) by reference to UN R138. It is a definition only, and the rear lamp spec includes no acoustic alerting system.
Paragraph 2.32 defines Accident Emergency Call Systems (AECS) by reference to UN R144. It is a definition only, and the rear lamp spec includes no emergency call system.
Paragraph 2.33 defines Auxiliary Equipment (AE) as equipment used to exercise or monitor a test object. It is a test-related definition with no obligation for the product.
Paragraph 2.34 defines the lowest usable frequency (LUF), a term for EMC field-uniformity testing. It is a definition only and creates no obligation for the rear lamp.
Paragraph 3 is only a heading for the application-for-approval section and imposes no obligation on the product.
Paragraph 3.1 is a heading for vehicle-type approval and imposes no obligation on the product.

Paragraph 3.1.1 requires the vehicle manufacturer to submit an EMC type-approval application for a vehicle type. The product is a rear lamp component, not a vehicle type, and the spec gives no vehicle-level EMC application. The obligation falls on the vehicle manufacturer, not on this lamp.

3.1.2 concerns the vehicle type-approval information document (Annex 2A) submitted for vehicle EMC approval. The product is a rear lamp module, a component fitted to an M1 vehicle, not the vehicle type being approved, so this vehicle-level obligation does not attach to the lamp.

3.1.3 requires the vehicle manufacturer to draw up a schedule of vehicle electrical/electronic systems, body styles and wiring. This is a vehicle-level duty, and the spec describes only a rear lamp, not a vehicle schedule.
3.1.4 covers selection of a representative vehicle from the manufacturer's schedule for vehicle type approval. It does not apply to a standalone rear lamp component.
3.1.5 limits representative vehicle choice to production combinations. This is a vehicle type-approval procedure and does not apply to the rear lamp component.
3.1.6 is an optional vehicle-approval test report supplement. It is a vehicle application procedure and does not create product obligations for the rear lamp.
3.1.7 requires a representative vehicle to be provided when the Technical Service tests a vehicle. This is a vehicle test-logistics provision and does not apply to the lamp component.

3.1.8 requires vehicle manufacturers of M-category vehicles to state RF transmitter frequency bands and installation provisions. The obligation sits with the vehicle manufacturer, and the rear lamp spec describes no RF transmitter.
3.2 is a section heading for ESA type approval. It creates no independent obligation.

3.2.1 states the applicability of the regulation to ESAs, but its limiting sub-items are not in the retrieved text. Whether the rear lamp's LED/PCB electronics count as an ESA under 2.8 depends on that limitation. The spec gives no detail on the lamp's electronic content beyond LED modules on PCB.

decisions.reason: Annex 4 para 2.1.1 sets engine operation conditions for vehicle radiated-emission testing (CISPR 12, electric propulsion, traction motors). The product is a rear lamp module, a lighting component with LED modules, not a vehicle propulsion system or engine, so this test-state condition does not apply.

Para 2.1.2 concerns operating other vehicle systems such as wiper motors and fans during vehicle EMC testing. The rear lamp spec describes no such broadband-emitting equipment; it is a passive-plus-LED lighting module within a vehicle, and this vehicle-level test state does not govern the lamp.

Para 2.2 defines the vehicle test configuration 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid'. The rear lamp has no REESS, charging plug or grid connection, so this configuration does not apply to the product.

Figure 1 is the flowchart for selecting the charging-mode test configuration of a vehicle with REESS charging. The rear lamp spec has no battery, charging mode or charging connection, so the flowchart does not apply.

Para 2.2.1 covers vehicles in charging mode 1 or 2 (AC charging without communication). The rear lamp is not a vehicle capable of charging and has no charging interface, so this scope does not match the product.
Para 2.2.1.1 sets the power-mains socket placement for charging-mode EMC tests. The rear lamp has no mains charging connection, so this test-setup requirement does not apply.
Para 2.2.1.2 requires 50 µH/50 Ω artificial networks for mains-connected charging tests. The rear lamp is not connected to mains power, so this test requirement does not apply.
Para 2.2.1.3 sets power charging harness routing for charging-mode EMC tests. The product spec describes no charging harness, so this requirement does not apply.
Para 2.2.2 covers vehicles in charging mode 3 or 4 (AC/DC charging with communication). The rear lamp has no charging function or communication with a charging station, so this scope does not match.

Para 2.2.2.1 sets charging-station and power-mains socket conditions for communication-enabled charging tests. The rear lamp has no charging station or communication interface, so this requirement does not apply.
Para 2.2.2.2 specifies AC and DC artificial networks for charging-mode tests. The rear lamp is not a charging-connected vehicle or ESA, so this test network requirement does not apply.

Para 2.2.2.3 specifies asymmetric artificial networks for local/private communication lines to a charging station. The rear lamp has no signal/control or wired network ports for charging communication, so this requirement does not apply.

Annex 4 / 2.2.2.4 sets harness layout for a vehicle in AC/DC power charging mode with communication, between AMN/AN units and the vehicle charging socket. The product is a rear lamp module (position, stop, reversing lamps, outer lens, retro-reflector) with no charging socket, charging harness, or REESS charging function in the specification.

Annex 4 / 3 is only a heading for the measuring location of the vehicle emissions test. The rear lamp is not a vehicle subject to this charging-mode radiated emission test, so there is no obligation for this product.

Annex 4 / 3.1 gives an alternative test surface for CISPR 12 measurements, expressly for vehicles of category L. The product is a rear lamp component for an M1 passenger car, and the specification describes no emissions test setup or vehicle-level measurement.
Annex 4 / 3.2 permits ALSE or OTS test sites for vehicle radiated emission measurements. It is a test-facility choice for vehicles and does not impose any obligation on a rear lamp module.

Annex 4 / 4 is a heading for the vehicle test requirements of the charging-mode emission method. The rear lamp module has no charging configuration or radiated emission test in its specification, so the heading creates no obligation for it.

Annex 4 / 4.1 sets emission limits from 30 to 1,000 MHz for vehicle measurements in an ALSE or OTS. The rear lamp's functions (signalling, braking, reversing light, retro-reflection) involve no charging emissions, and the specification gives no EMC emission data for this product.

Annex 4 / 4.2 covers the choice of quasi-peak or peak detectors and their correction factor for vehicle emission measurements. It is a measurement procedure for vehicles in charging mode, which does not apply to the rear lamp module described.

Annex 4 / 4.3 specifies the spectrum analyser or scanning receiver measurement method for the vehicle emission test. The rear lamp specification includes no such measurement, and the clause does not govern a passive lamp component.
Table 1 lists spectrum analyser parameters for the vehicle radiated emission test in Annex 4. It is a test-equipment specification with no product-specific obligation for a rear lamp.
Table 2 lists scanning receiver parameters for the vehicle radiated emission test in Annex 4. It is a test-equipment table with no product-specific obligation for a rear lamp.

Annex 4 / 4.4 covers how the Technical Service performs vehicle emission measurements across 30 to 1,000 MHz, including REESS charging-mode configurations. The rear lamp has no charging-mode configuration and is not a vehicle under test in this procedure.
Annex 4 / 4.5 defines how vehicle emission readings are taken relative to the limits. It is a vehicle test-reading procedure with no applicability to the rear lamp module.

Annex 4 para 4.6 sets antenna positions for radiated broadband emission measurements on a vehicle (left/right sides, distance to vehicle body, vehicle length L). The product is a rear lamp module (a component), not a complete vehicle, so there is no vehicle measurement set-up to apply it to.

Figure 1 depicts the clear horizontal test surface for the vehicle radiated emission measurement in Annex 4. It is a test-site figure for vehicles and does not impose any obligation on a rear lamp module.
Figure 2 shows the antenna position relative to the vehicle for the Annex 4 vehicle measurement. The product is a rear lamp, not a vehicle under test, so this set-up does not apply.

Figure 3 covers the test set-up for a vehicle in the 'REESS charging mode' coupled to the power grid (AC/DC charging, AMN, EVSE). The rear lamp specification has no charging coupling, REESS or charging function, so this does not apply.
Figure 4 shows the antenna position for N=1 with a vehicle under test. The product is a rear lamp module and is not a vehicle under test, so this set-up does not apply.
Figure 5 shows multiple antenna positions (N=2) for a vehicle under test in Annex 4. The rear lamp is a component and not a vehicle, so this set-up does not apply.
Annex 5 is the method for measuring radiated narrowband emissions from vehicles. The product is a rear lamp component, not a vehicle, so the method does not apply to it.
This is the general heading of Annex 5 ('1. General') for the vehicle narrowband emission test. It creates no obligation for a rear lamp component.

Annex 5 para 1.1 states the method 'shall only be applied to vehicles' and excludes the REESS charging configuration. The rear lamp is not a vehicle and has no charging configuration, so this does not apply.
Annex 5 para 1.2 gives the narrowband emission test method (CISPR 12) for vehicles. It is a vehicle test method, and the rear lamp component is not a vehicle, so it does not apply.

Annex 5 para 1.3 concerns the measurement location for vehicles of category L. The product is a rear lamp for an M1 passenger car, not a vehicle of category L, and it is not a vehicle, so this does not apply.

1. SCOPE
This Regulation applies to LED light sources shown in Annex 1 and intended for use in approved lamps of power-

decisions.reason: Paragraph 4.1.5 is a packaging-marking requirement for LED substitute light sources. The rear lamp spec describes an integrated lamp module (rear position, stop, reversing, retro-reflector, outer lens) with LED modules on a PCB, not a separately packaged substitute light source. The spec mentions no package, marking, or retrofit sale.

Paragraph 4.2 requires instructions packed with each LED substitute light source package. The scope (Scope, paragraph 1) covers LED light sources intended for use in approved lamps, which the spec does not describe as a separately sold substitute. No packaging or instructions are mentioned in the spec.

Paragraph 4.2.1 concerns package statements that a LED substitute light source is suitable for fitment in vehicle lamps. The rear lamp is an integrated vehicle lamp, not a substitute light source with a package. The spec does not describe a substitute source or its packaging.

Paragraph 4.2.2 requires the LED substitute light source manufacturer to publish fitment listings on a website. This applies to aftermarket substitute sources. The spec describes a rear lamp module and does not indicate a substitute light source or such a manufacturer listing.

Paragraph 4.2.3 is a package-information requirement for LED substitute light sources, referring to vehicle lamp markings. The spec does not describe a substitute source package, so this clause does not apply.

Paragraph 4.2.4 is a package-information requirement for LED substitute light sources, referring users to repair shops when applicability is unclear. The spec does not describe a substitute source package, so this clause does not apply.

Paragraph 4.2.5 is a warning for the packaging of LED substitute light sources about misuse in vehicle electrical systems. The spec does not describe a substitute light source package, so this clause does not apply.

Paragraph 4.3 requires the manufacturer to display the paragraph 4.2 instructions at the point of sale without opening the package. This is a retail-display obligation for LED substitute light source packages, which the rear lamp spec does not describe.

Paragraph 5 is only the heading for the conformity of production section for LED light sources approved to UN R128. The spec does not state that the rear lamp or its LED modules are approved under UN R128.

Paragraph 5.1 requires LED light sources approved to UN R128 to conform to the type approval, and packaging information to conform to paragraph 4. The spec describes a rear lamp assembly, not an LED light source approved under UN R128, and it does not mention an R128 approval. The clause therefore does not apply on the available evidence.

Paragraph 5.2 requires production controls to verify paragraph 4.1 requirements, which concern packaging information for LED substitute light sources. The spec does not describe such packaging or an R128 approval, so the clause does not apply.

Paragraph 5.3 places quality-control and testing duties on the holder of an UN R128 LED light source approval. The spec describes a rear lamp module for an M1 vehicle, with no indication that it is an R128-approved LED light source or that its holder has such an approval. The obligations do not apply on the available evidence.

Clause 5.3.7 is a record-keeping duty for the holder of an R128 LED light source approval. R128 scope (clause 1) covers LED light sources intended for approved lamps. The spec describes a complete rear lamp with 'LED modules on PCB' but does not say those modules hold a separate R128 approval. Applicability is therefore unconfirmed.

decisions.reason: Introduction to UN R131 on Advanced Emergency Braking Systems for M2, M3, N2 and N3 vehicles. It is background only and imposes no obligation. The product is a rear lamp module for an M1 passenger car, with no braking-system or AEBS function.
Scope limits approval to vehicles of Category M2, M3, N2 and N3 for an on-board AEBS. The product spec states the vehicle is M1, and the product is a lamp module, not an AEBS.
Heading for the definitions section only. It has no obligation and no product scope, and the product is not an AEBS-equipped vehicle.

Defines Advanced Emergency Braking System. The rear lamp (rear position, stop, reversing lamps, retro-reflector, outer lens) does not perform forward collision detection or braking, so this definition does not apply to the product.
Defines Emergency Braking as a braking demand from AEBS to the service brake. The product's stop lamp is a signalling function, not an emergency braking demand, and the product has no AEBS.
Defines Collision Warning emitted by AEBS to the driver. The product's rear lamps give signals to other road users, not an AEBS collision warning to the driver.
Defines vehicle type with regard to its AEBS. It concerns AEBS vehicle type approval families and does not apply to a rear lamp module.
Defines Subject Vehicle as the vehicle under AEBS test. It is a test-terminology definition with no bearing on the rear lamp product.
Defines Soft Target for AEBS collision testing. It has no bearing on the rear lamp product.
Defines Vehicle Target for AEBS testing. It has no bearing on the rear lamp product.
Defines Pedestrian Target for AEBS testing. It has no bearing on the rear lamp product.
Defines Common Space for displayed information functions, such as in AEBS driver interfaces. The rear lamp product has no display or information function of this kind.

Paragraph 3.3 requires submitting a representative vehicle to the Technical Service for AEBS approval tests. UN R131 covers AEBS on M2, M3, N2 and N3 vehicles (scope, paragraph 1). The product is a rear lamp module for an M1 passenger car, not an AEBS or a vehicle type under this regulation.
Paragraph 4 is the approval heading for the UN R131 AEBS regulation. The product is a rear lamp, and the regulation's scope does not cover M1 vehicles or lighting components.
Paragraph 4.1 grants approval of a vehicle type that meets the AEBS requirements of paragraph 5. The product is a rear lamp on an M1 car, which is outside UN R131's AEBS scope (M2, M3, N2, N3).
Paragraph 4.2 concerns the approval number for a vehicle type equipped with AEBS. The product spec describes a rear lamp, not an AEBS-equipped vehicle type under UN R131.
Paragraph 4.3 covers communication of AEBS approval notices between Contracting Parties. It is an administrative clause with no product obligation, and it does not apply to the rear lamp.

Paragraph 4.4 requires an international approval mark on vehicles approved under UN R131 (AEBS). The rear lamp spec does not indicate a UN R131 vehicle type approval, and the regulation's scope does not include M1 vehicles.
Paragraph 4.4.1 describes the content of the approval mark (the E-circle and country number) for UN R131 AEBS approvals. It does not apply to the rear lamp product.
Paragraph 4.4.2 describes the regulation number and approval number shown beside the approval mark for UN R131 approvals. It is not applicable to the rear lamp product.

Paragraph 4.5 covers the placement of approval symbols when a vehicle is approved under several regulations. It is an approval-marking clause for UN R131 vehicles and does not apply to a rear lamp component.
Paragraph 4.6 requires the UN R131 approval mark to be legible and indelible. The product is a rear lamp, not a vehicle carrying a UN R131 AEBS approval mark.
Paragraph 4.7 requires the UN R131 approval mark to be placed near the vehicle data plate. The product is a rear lamp and the regulation does not apply to it.

Paragraph 5 is the heading for the UN R131 AEBS performance specifications. The regulation covers AEBS on M2, M3, N2, N3 vehicles, and the rear lamp (M1 passenger car, lighting and signalling) is outside that scope.

Paragraph 5.1 sets general requirements for AEBS under UN R131. R131 scope (paragraph 1) covers AEBS on M2, M3, N2 and N3 vehicles. The product is a rear lamp module for an M1 passenger car, and the specification mentions no AEBS, so this clause does not apply to the product.
Paragraph 5.1.1 applies only to vehicles fitted with an AEBS. The rear lamp specification describes no AEBS, and the vehicle category (M1) is outside R131 scope.
Paragraph 5.1.2 concerns the immunity of AEBS to magnetic and electrical fields. The rear lamp is not an AEBS, and the specification does not describe one.
Paragraph 5.1.3 concerns electronic control system safety for AEBS under Annex 3. The rear lamp's LED modules are light sources, not an AEBS control system, and the vehicle is outside R131 scope.
Paragraph 5.1.4 sets driver warning requirements for AEBS. The rear lamp specification contains no AEBS or driver warning function.
Paragraph 5.1.4.1 requires an AEBS failure warning. The rear lamp has no AEBS, so this does not apply.
Paragraph 5.1.4.1.1 concerns AEBS self-check and warning illumination timing. The product has no AEBS.
Paragraph 5.1.4.1.2 concerns AEBS non-electrical failure warnings such as sensor blindness. The product has no AEBS sensors or warning system.
Paragraph 5.1.4.2 concerns AEBS initialisation status information to the driver. The rear lamp has no AEBS.
Paragraph 5.1.4.3 concerns an AEBS deactivation warning. The rear lamp has no AEBS.
Paragraph 5.1.5 concerns AEBS emergency braking interventions. The rear lamp's stop lamp signals braking to others but does not perform vehicle braking intervention, and the product has no AEBS.

Paragraph 2.8 defines a "component of the braking equipment". The rear lamp's parts (lens, reflector, light sources) are not components of a vehicle braking system, so this definition does not apply.
Paragraph 2.9 defines "progressive and graduated braking" as a property of brake control. The rear lamp has no braking force control, so this does not apply.
Paragraph 2.9.1 is a sub-criterion of progressive braking (driver adjusts braking force). The rear lamp produces no braking force, so this does not apply.
Paragraph 2.9.2 is a sub-criterion of progressive braking (braking force proportional to control action). The rear lamp produces no braking force, so this does not apply.
Paragraph 2.9.3 is a sub-criterion of progressive braking (braking force easily regulated). The rear lamp produces no braking force, so this does not apply.
Paragraph 2.10 defines "laden vehicle" by reference to maximum mass. It is a vehicle-loading definition used for braking tests and has no bearing on a rear lamp module.
Paragraph 2.11 defines "maximum mass" for vehicle loading. The rear lamp spec contains no mass-related obligation, so this definition does not apply to the product.

Defines 'distribution of mass among the axles' for braking regulation UN R13H, which covers braking of M1/N1 vehicles. The rear lamp spec (position, stop, reversing lamps, retro-reflector, lens) has no braking-system or axle-mass function, so the definition does not apply to this product.
Defines 'wheel/axle load' as a braking-regulation term. The rear lamp spec describes no wheel, axle, or road-contact function, so this definition does not apply to the product.
Defines 'maximum stationary wheel/axle load' for braking purposes. The rear lamp spec contains no axle-load function, so this definition does not apply.
Defines hydraulic braking equipment with stored energy. The rear lamp is a lighting and signalling module with no hydraulic or braking equipment, so the definition does not apply.
Defines 'actuation' of a braking control. The rear lamp spec lists no control actuated by the driver for braking, so this definition does not apply.

Defines electric regenerative braking. The rear lamp spec describes an LED lighting module with no braking-energy conversion function, so this definition does not apply. The stop lamp is a light function, not a braking system.
Defines an electric regenerative braking control device. The product spec has no such device, so this definition does not apply.
Defines category A electric regenerative braking system. The product spec has no braking system of any kind, so this definition does not apply.
Defines category B electric regenerative braking system. The product spec has no braking system, so this definition does not apply.

Defines electric State of Charge for energy storage devices such as traction batteries. The rear lamp spec describes LED modules on PCB with no traction battery or energy-storage function, so this definition does not apply.
Defines a traction battery for powering traction motors. The rear lamp spec has no traction battery or traction motor, so this definition does not apply.
Defines phased braking for combined braking sources operated from a common control. The rear lamp spec has no braking control or braking sources, so this definition does not apply.

Defines "nominal value" for the braking system's transfer function. The rear lamp spec describes lighting and signalling functions only, with no braking system, so the term does not apply to this product.
Defines "nominal value" as braking rate versus braking input for type approval of the vehicle's braking. The rear lamp spec has no braking-rate or braking-input characteristic.
Defines "automatically commanded braking" within a vehicle's electronic control system. The rear lamp spec describes no braking control function, so the definition does not apply.
Defines "selective braking" (actuation of individual brakes). The rear lamp spec describes no brake actuation, so the definition does not apply.

Defines a "braking signal" as a logic signal for brake activation under R13H para 5.2.22. This is a vehicle braking-system signal definition. The stop lamp is a light function, but the spec does not describe a braking-system logic signal, and this definition imposes no obligation on the lamp hardware.

Defines an "emergency braking signal" under R13H para 5.2.23. Its scope is the vehicle braking system, and the rear lamp spec does not mention emergency braking logic. The ADS/DDT text in the same numbered block is not part of this definition's scope for this product.
Defines "brake demand value" for electrically actuated wheel or axle braking. The rear lamp spec has no electrically actuated brake, so the definition does not apply.
Defines the performance of an electrical storage device (W and Wh) for a braking system. The rear lamp spec lists LED modules on PCB as light source and no electrical storage device for braking.
Defines "Pw" as the low electrical supply power warning for an electrical transmission braking system. The rear lamp spec has no braking transmission system, so the definition does not apply.
Defines an "energy source" for the braking system. The rear lamp spec does not describe any energy source for braking, so the definition does not apply.
Defines "electrical storage device" for supplying the braking system transmission. The rear lamp spec describes no such device or braking circuit, so the definition does not apply.
Defines the "effect of ageing" for an electrical storage device in a braking system. The rear lamp spec describes no electrical storage device, so the definition does not apply.

Defines 'Electrical supply' for the braking system's electrical storage devices. R13H governs braking of M1/N1 vehicles, and the rear lamp spec describes a lighting module with no braking-system or electrical-storage role, so this definition does not apply to the product.
Defines 'Energy Management System' for electrical transmission braking systems. The rear lamp spec has no braking transmission or energy management function.
Defines 'Electrical Transmission Braking System' (ETBS). The product is a rear lamp with stop-lamp signalling only, not a service braking system.
Defines 'Auxiliary equipment' in the braking context and 'Identification code' for brake discs or drums. Neither relates to the rear lamp, which has no brake discs, drums, or braking energy reserves.
Defines the 'state of an electrical storage device' in braking terms (power and energy). The rear lamp spec does not include a braking electrical storage device.
Defines 'Reference braking forces' measured on a roller brake tester. This is a braking performance concept with no bearing on a rear lamp.
Defines the 'Electronic vehicle interface' for real-time braking-system parameters. The rear lamp spec has no such interface.
Section heading 'Application for approval' for vehicle braking type approval. It imposes no obligation on the rear lamp and is not a product requirement.

Requires the vehicle manufacturer to apply for braking-type approval. This is an administrative obligation on the vehicle type, not on the rear lamp component, and the spec does not describe a braking approval.
Requires an application package in triplicate with braking particulars. This is a type-approval documentation obligation for the braking system, not a rear lamp product requirement.
Requires a description of the vehicle type with regard to braking items in paragraph 2.2. This is vehicle braking documentation and does not apply to the rear lamp module.
Requires a list of components constituting the braking equipment. The rear lamp is not braking equipment; its stop-lamp function is a light signal, and R13H does not regulate lamp components.

Paragraph 3.2.3 requires a diagram of the assembled braking equipment for a vehicle type approval application. UN R13H covers vehicle braking for M1 and N1 vehicles (clause 1.1). The specified rear lamp is an exterior lighting and signalling module, not braking equipment under this Regulation, so this documentation requirement does not apply to it.

Paragraph 3.2.4 requires detailed drawings of braking-equipment components in a vehicle braking approval dossier. The rear lamp is a lighting module outside the braking equipment scope of UN R13H, so this requirement does not apply to the product.

Paragraph 3.3 requires a representative vehicle to be submitted for braking approval tests. This is a vehicle braking approval procedure. The product specification describes a rear lamp module, and the stop lamp is a signalling function, not a braking system component tested under this Regulation.
Paragraph 4 is a section heading for the approval of vehicle braking equipment. It creates no product obligation for the rear lamp.

Paragraph 4.1 grants approval of a vehicle type under UN R13H when braking requirements in paragraphs 5 and 6 are met. It concerns braking approval of the vehicle type, not the rear lamp module described in the specification.
Paragraph 4.2 concerns the numbering of braking-equipment approvals. The product is a rear lamp and is not a braking equipment type under this Regulation, so the numbering rule does not apply.
Paragraph 4.3 concerns notification of braking approval or refusal and the documents supplied for it. It does not impose an obligation on the rear lamp product.

Paragraph 4.4 requires an international approval mark on each vehicle conforming to a UN R13H braking vehicle type approval. The rear lamp module is not a vehicle conforming to this approval, so the mark requirement does not apply to the product.

Paragraph 4.4.1 specifies the content of the international approval mark (the E circle and country number) for a UN R13H braking vehicle approval. The rear lamp module is not a vehicle conforming to this approval, so the mark content does not apply to the product.

Paragraph 4.4.2 specifies the regulation number, letter R and approval number format for the approval mark of a UN R13H braking vehicle approval. The rear lamp module is not that approved vehicle, so this does not apply to the product.
Paragraph 4.5 covers the placement of approval numbers when a vehicle conforms to other regulations. It concerns vehicle approval marking under UN R13H, not the rear lamp module.

Paragraph 4.6 requires the approval mark to be legible and indelible. The approval mark belongs to a UN R13H braking approval of a vehicle type. The rear lamp module is not that approved vehicle, so the requirement does not apply to the product.

decisions.reason: Paragraph 4.7 places the approval mark for the R13H braking-of-vehicles approval close to or on the vehicle data plate. The product is a rear lamp module (position, stop, reversing lamps, outer lens, retro-reflector), not a vehicle braking approval subject, so this marking obligation does not apply to it.

Paragraph 4.8 only refers to Annex 2 examples of approval mark arrangements for R13H braking approvals. It imposes no obligation on the rear lamp and the product spec describes no braking-system approval.

Section 5 is a heading for the braking specifications of UN R13H. Its scope (scope 1.1) is the braking of M1 and N1 vehicles. The rear lamp spec describes lighting and signalling functions, not vehicle braking equipment.

Paragraph 5.1 is a general heading for vehicle braking specifications. The product is a rear lamp with a stop lamp function, but the R13H braking requirements apply to the vehicle braking equipment, not to the lamp module, so this heading does not apply.

Paragraph 5.1.1 heading covers braking equipment of the vehicle. The product spec has no service, secondary, or parking brake equipment; its stop lamp only indicates braking and is not a braking equipment item under this Regulation.

Paragraph 5.1.1.1 requires vehicle braking equipment to withstand vibration in normal use. The rear lamp spec does not describe any braking equipment; the stop lamp is a signalling light and not a braking component.

Paragraph 5.1.1.2 requires braking equipment to resist corrosion and ageing. The rear lamp's materials (PMMA, PP/ASA/PC, aluminium coating) are not braking equipment under this clause, so it does not apply to the lamp.
Paragraph 5.1.1.3 prohibits asbestos in brake linings. The rear lamp spec has no brake linings and no friction material, so the clause does not apply.

Paragraph 5.1.1.4 concerns magnetic and electrical field effects on braking effectiveness. The rear lamp is an LED lighting module, not braking equipment, so the braking-effectiveness requirement does not apply to it.
Paragraph 5.1.1.5 concerns momentary interruption of the demand signal in braking control transmission. The rear lamp spec has no braking control transmission, so this clause does not apply.
Paragraph 5.1.2 defines the functions of the braking equipment defined in paragraph 2.3. The rear lamp is not braking equipment, so these functional requirements do not apply to the product.

Paragraph 5.1.2.1 sets the service braking system function (controlling and halting the vehicle). The rear lamp spec describes no service brake system; its stop lamp is only a signal and does not perform braking, so this clause does not apply.

Paragraph 5.1.2.2 sets performance requirements for the vehicle's secondary braking system, which is part of the vehicle braking equipment. Regulation UN R13H (scope 1.1) covers braking of M1 and N1 vehicles. The rear lamp spec (position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp, outer lens, retro-reflector) is a lighting and signalling module and has no braking-system function in this sense. The stop lamp only signals braking and does not perform braking, so this clause does not apply.
Paragraph 5.1.2.3 concerns the parking braking system's mechanical hold function. The product is a rear lamp module with no parking brake function, so the clause does not apply to this product.

Paragraph 5.1.3 applies Annex 8 to complex electronic vehicle control systems that form part of the braking control transmission. The rear lamp spec describes no electronic brake control system. Its stop lamp is only a signal output and is not part of the braking control chain.
Paragraph 5.1.4 is a heading for periodic technical inspection provisions for braking systems. It creates no obligation, and the rear lamp has no braking system to inspect.

Paragraph 5.1.4.1 requires the wear condition of service brake components (friction linings, drums, discs) to be assessable. The rear lamp spec contains no friction or wear components, so the clause does not apply.
Paragraph 5.1.4.2 concerns generating maximum braking forces on a roller brake tester. The rear lamp is not a braking component and is not tested on a brake tester, so the clause does not apply.
Paragraph 5.1.4.3 is a heading for data requirements on braking systems. It creates no obligation, and the rear lamp spec describes no braking system data.

Paragraph 5.1.4.3.1 requires braking-system test data for an electrical transmission braking system to be specified at the vehicle. The rear lamp spec describes no electrical transmission braking system, so the clause does not apply.

Paragraph 5.1.4.3.2 concerns the manufacturer's procedure for checking detection means that trigger braking warning signals on vehicles with an electrical transmission braking system. The rear lamp spec describes no such braking warning system or detection means, so the clause does not apply.
Paragraph 5.1.4.3.3 concerns park lock devices and the axle they act on. The rear lamp spec contains no park lock device, so the clause does not apply.
Paragraph 5.1.4.4 is a heading for reference braking forces. It creates no obligation, and the rear lamp has no braking force to reference.

Paragraph 5.1.4.4.1 defines reference braking forces for an electrical transmission braking system on a roller brake tester. The rear lamp spec describes no braking system, so the clause does not apply.

Paragraph 5.1.4.4.1.1 covers roller brake tester evaluation and display of brake demand values for vehicle braking systems. The product is a rear lamp module (position, stop, reversing lamps, outer lens, retro-reflector), so this braking-system inspection requirement does not apply.
Paragraph 5.1.4.4.1.2 sets reference braking forces per axle for vehicle braking. The rear lamp specification contains no braking-force or brake-system content, so it does not apply.
Paragraph 5.1.4.1.3 concerns declared reference braking forces and vehicle braking rate. The product is a rear lamp, not a braking system or vehicle, so this clause does not apply.

Paragraph 5.1.4.5 concerns verification of electronic systems that control braking. The rear lamp spec describes no electronic braking control; its only electronic element is LED modules on a PCB used for light output, so this does not apply.

Paragraph 5.1.4.5.1 concerns visual confirmation of braking-system warning signals at periodic inspection. The rear lamp is a stop/position/reversing lighting module and is not a braking warning or control system, so this does not apply.

Paragraph 5.1.4.5.2 concerns protection of braking-system verification means against unauthorised modification. The rear lamp specification does not include any braking control or verification means, so this does not apply.
Paragraph 5.2 is a heading for characteristics of braking systems. It creates no obligation for a rear lamp.
Paragraph 5.2.1 requires the braking systems of a vehicle to meet service, secondary and parking brake requirements. The rear lamp is not a braking system, so this does not apply to the product.
Paragraph 5.2.2 concerns common components of service, secondary and parking braking systems. The rear lamp contains no braking-system components, so this does not apply.
Paragraph 5.2.2.1 concerns brake controls readily accessible to the driver and their return to the off position. The rear lamp is not a brake control, so this does not apply.
Paragraph 5.2.2.2 requires independence between service and parking brake controls. The rear lamp has no brake controls or parking brake, so this does not apply.
Paragraph 5.2.2.3 concerns the linkage between the service brake control and transmission components. The rear lamp contains no brake linkage, so this does not apply.

5.2.2.4 requires the parking braking system to be actuable while the vehicle is in motion. The rear lamp spec covers only position, stop, reversing lamps, outer lens and retro-reflector, with no parking brake or braking transmission. The stop lamp is a signalling function, not part of the braking system.
5.2.2.5 concerns shared service and parking brake transmission components and secondary braking after transmission failure. The rear lamp spec has no brake transmission or braking components.
5.2.2.7 concerns secondary braking when the driver's muscular energy is assisted by energy reserves. The rear lamp spec has no service brake control or energy-assisted braking.
5.2.2.8 concerns independent energy reserves for service braking transmission. The rear lamp spec has no energy reserve or braking transmission.
5.2.2.9 concerns a single energy reserve for braking transmission. The rear lamp spec has no braking energy reserve.

5.2.2.10 concerns material and robustness of brake components such as pedals, master cylinders and brake cylinders. The rear lamp spec lists no brake components; its materials (PMMA lens, PP/ASA/PC housing, retro-reflector) are lighting parts.

5.2.3 concerns a red brake-failure tell-tale for hydraulic transmission faults. The rear lamp spec describes no hydraulic braking system and no brake failure warning; the stop lamp is a braking indication to other road users, not a brake-system tell-tale.
5.2.4 concerns energy supply for braking systems (pumps, compressors). The rear lamp spec includes no braking energy supply.
5.2.4.1 concerns feed continuity to braking transmission parts after failure. The rear lamp spec has no braking transmission.
5.2.4.2 concerns stored energy in braking circuits and the fifth-application stopping test. The rear lamp spec has no stored braking energy.
5.2.4.3 is an alternative compliance route for hydraulic braking systems with stored energy. The rear lamp spec has no hydraulic braking system.
5.2.4.4 is an alternative for electrical transmission braking systems. The rear lamp spec describes lighting only, not an electrical brake transmission.

Clause 5.2.4.4.1 sets energy-supply and electrical-transmission braking requirements for the vehicle's service braking system. The rear lamp spec covers only lighting and signalling functions (position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp, outer lens, retro-reflector) and has no braking system or energy supply. The stop lamp is a signalling device, not a brake component, so this clause does not apply.
Clause 5.2.5 concerns automatic devices in the braking system that act only on failure. The rear lamp spec has no braking system, so it does not apply.
Clause 5.2.6 requires the service braking system to act on all wheels. The rear lamp is a lighting module and has no braking action on wheels, so it does not apply.
Clause 5.2.7 covers phasing of electric regenerative braking in vehicles. The rear lamp spec does not include any braking or regenerative system, so it does not apply.
Clause 5.2.7.1 covers compensation for regenerative braking torque variation. The rear lamp spec does not include a regenerative braking system, so it does not apply.
Clause 5.2.7.2 requires declaration of braking-rate compensation functions. The rear lamp spec has no braking-rate compensation function, so it does not apply.
Clause 5.2.8 covers symmetric distribution of service brake action between wheels of an axle. The rear lamp spec has no brake action, so it does not apply.

Clause 5.2.8.1 covers brake pressure compensation limits and the yellow warning signal for braking-system deterioration. The rear lamp spec does not include a braking system or brake warning function, so it does not apply. The stop lamp is not the yellow braking-compensation warning.
Clause 5.2.8.1.2 sets limits on individual compensating values in the braking system. The rear lamp spec has no braking compensation, so it does not apply.

Clause 5.2.8.2 limits compensation to initial brake application above 10 km/h, and clause 5.2.9 prevents electric control transmission malfunctions from applying brakes. The rear lamp spec has no braking control transmission, so neither applies.
Clause 5.2.10 covers braking-surface connections, park lock devices, and parking brake disconnection. The rear lamp spec has no braking or parking brake system, so it does not apply.
Clause 5.2.11 covers brake wear adjustment and reserve of travel in the braking system. The rear lamp spec has no brakes, so it does not apply.

Clause 5.2.11.1 sets automatic wear adjustment requirements for the service brakes of a vehicle. The product is a rear lamp module (position, stop, reversing lamps, lens, retro-reflector) and the spec contains no brake, wear adjuster, or braking-system component. The regulation's scope covers vehicle braking, so this clause does not apply to the lamp.

Paragraph 1.5 is only a cross-reference to a Type-I test for braking performance. It belongs to the braking-system test regime, and the rear lamp spec has no braking system to test. The numbering flag does not change this outcome.
Clause 5.2.11.2 is a heading for checking wear of service brake friction components. The rear lamp has no friction components or brake linings, so it does not apply.

Clause 5.2.11.2.1 requires that brake lining wear be assessable from outside the vehicle, or that a sensing device warn the driver. This concerns service brake linings. The rear lamp spec contains no brake linings or wear sensor, so it does not apply.
Clause 5.2.11.2.2 concerns the wear of brake disc or drum friction surfaces and manufacturer wear-limit information. The rear lamp has no brake discs or drums, so it does not apply.
Clause 5.2.12 covers reserve fluid reservoirs in hydraulic braking systems. The rear lamp spec has no hydraulic braking system or fluid reservoir, so it does not apply.
Clause 5.2.13 requires a brake fluid type symbol and DOT marking near the fluid filling ports. The rear lamp has no brake fluid or filling port, so it does not apply.
Clause 5.2.14 is a heading for the braking-system warning device requirements. The rear lamp has no braking energy reserve or warning device, so it does not apply.

Clause 5.2.14.1 requires a warning device for a service brake actuated from an energy reserve. The product is a rear lamp module with no energy-reserve brake system. Its red warning signal refers to the dashboard braking warning, not the rear stop lamp, so it does not apply.
Clause 5.2.14.1.4 concerns whether an acoustic brake warning device may be disabled while the parking brake is applied. The rear lamp has no acoustic braking warning device, so it does not apply.

Clause 5.2.14.2 requires an acoustic plus optical brake warning in certain vehicles. It concerns the braking system's warning devices, not the rear lamp. The spec describes no braking warning device, so it does not apply.

Clause 5.2.14.3 requires an acoustic signal for vehicles with an electrical transmission braking system. The rear lamp has no electrical transmission braking system or storage-device warning, so it does not apply.

Paragraph 5.2.14.4 applies to vehicles equipped with an electrical transmission braking system and requires a storage-device ageing indicator. The product is a rear lamp module (position, stop, reversing lamps, lens, retro-reflector), not a braking system or vehicle braking installation, so this clause does not apply to it.

Paragraph 5.2.14.4 continuation concerns the ageing indicator for electrical storage devices of electrical transmission braking systems. The rear lamp specification has no braking-system storage device or indicator, so it does not apply.

Paragraph 5.2.15 sets energy-reserve requirements for auxiliary energy sources of braking systems and parking brake servo devices. The rear lamp is not a braking component and has no auxiliary braking energy source, so this does not apply.

Paragraph 5.2.16 governs pneumatic, hydraulic or electrical auxiliary braking equipment and its effect on braking energy reserves. The rear lamp is not auxiliary braking equipment, so this does not apply.

Paragraph 5.2.17 is a heading for trailer-towing electric service brake requirements on motor vehicles. The product is a rear lamp module and not a vehicle braking or towing system, so it does not apply.

Paragraph 5.2.17.1 sets power-supply voltage and capacity requirements for trailer electric braking systems. The rear lamp specification does not describe a trailer electric braking system, so this does not apply.
Paragraph 5.2.17.2 concerns trailer braking capability when a vehicle service brake unit fails. The rear lamp is not a vehicle service braking unit, so this does not apply.

Paragraph 5.2.17.3 concerns using the stop-lamp switch and circuit to actuate an electric trailer braking system. The product includes a stop lamp as a light function, but the clause governs the vehicle braking control circuit and not the lamp module itself, and the specification gives no such circuit or trailer braking use.
Paragraph 5.2.18 is a heading for electric regenerative braking systems. The rear lamp has no regenerative braking system, so this does not apply.
Paragraph 5.2.18.1 is a heading for category A electric regenerative braking systems. The rear lamp is not a braking system, so this does not apply.
Paragraph 5.2.18.1.1 governs when electric regenerative braking is activated. The rear lamp has no regenerative braking function, so this does not apply.
Paragraph 5.2.18.2 is a heading for category B electric regenerative braking systems. The rear lamp is not a braking system, so this does not apply.

Clause 5.2.18.2.1 concerns the service braking system of vehicles with electric regenerative braking (category B). The product is a rear lamp module (position, stop, reversing lamps, outer lens, retro-reflector), not a braking system or its components, so the clause does not apply.

Clause 5.2.18.2.2 requires the service braking system to have one control device. This is a braking-system design rule. The rear lamp spec has no braking control device; its stop lamp only indicates braking and does not form part of the braking system.
Clause 5.2.18.2.3 covers service braking performance under motor disengagement and gear ratio. The rear lamp spec describes no braking-system or drivetrain function, so the clause does not apply.

Clause 5.2.18.2.4 requires a driver warning for failure of the electric braking distribution relation. This is a vehicle braking-system warning obligation. The rear lamp spec does not include a braking-distribution control or a brake warning function, so the clause does not apply to the lamp module.
Clause 5.2.18.3 applies to vehicles with electric regenerative braking systems. The rear lamp spec is a lighting component and does not include regenerative braking or acceleration-demand control.

Clause 5.2.18.4 concerns the immunity of electric braking operation to magnetic and electric fields. The rear lamp spec has no electric braking function. Its LED modules are lighting sources, not braking-system components, so the clause does not apply.
Clause 5.2.18.5 requires an anti-lock device to control the electric braking system on vehicles equipped with ABS. The rear lamp spec describes no anti-lock device or electric braking system.
Clause 5.2.18.6 concerns the state of charge of traction batteries. The rear lamp spec has no traction battery or energy storage function; its LED modules are lighting sources only.
Clause 5.2.19 is a heading for special requirements on the electric transmission of the parking braking system. The rear lamp spec has no parking brake or electric parking-brake transmission.

Clause 5.2.19.1 requires prevention of unintended parking-brake actuation after a failure in the electric transmission. The rear lamp spec describes no parking brake or electric transmission, so the clause does not apply.

Clause 5.2.19.2 covers parking-brake application from the driver's seat after control or wiring failure, with 8% gradient holding. The rear lamp spec has no parking brake, control, or ECU, so the clause does not apply.

Clause 5.2.19.2.1 requires a yellow driver warning for a break in the parking-brake electrical transmission. The rear lamp spec describes no parking-brake control or warning function. The lamp's own signalling functions are not this braking-system warning, so the clause does not apply.

Paragraph 5.2.21.1.2 sets yellow/red warning-signal behaviour for parking braking system wiring breaks in the vehicle's braking control. The product is a rear lamp module (position, stop, reversing lamps, outer lens, retro-reflector) with no parking brake, brake control transmission, or brake warning function in the specification.

Paragraph 5.2.19.3 governs auxiliary equipment supplied from the parking brake's electric transmission energy reserve. The rear lamp specification does not describe any parking brake energy supply or electric brake transmission.
Paragraph 5.2.19.4 concerns applying and releasing the parking brake after the ignition is switched off. The rear lamp has no parking brake or ignition-controlled braking function.
Paragraph 5.2.19.5 applies to parking braking systems containing a park lock device. The rear lamp specification contains no park lock or parking brake.

Paragraph 5.2.20 is a heading for special requirements for service braking systems with electric control transmission. The rear lamp is not a service braking system component, and the stop lamp is a light function, not the brake actuation system.

Paragraph 5.2.20.1 sets static braking force and brake application performance for the service braking system. The rear lamp specification does not include any braking force generation or service brake function.

Paragraph 5.2.20.2 concerns temporary failures in the service brake electric control transmission and their effect on braking performance. The rear lamp has no such control transmission in the specification.

Paragraph 5.2.20.3 requires failures in the electric control transmission of braking systems to be signalled via brake warning signals. The rear lamp specification describes no braking control transmission or brake warning signal.
Paragraph 5.2.20.4 covers the service brake control range after failure of the control transmission energy source. The rear lamp has no brake control or energy source of this kind.

Paragraph 5.2.20.5 relates to battery voltage thresholds for the service braking system and its red warning signal. The rear lamp specification does not describe battery voltage monitoring or a braking system.

Paragraph 5.2.20.6 addresses auxiliary equipment drawing from the electric control transmission reserve of the service brake system. The rear lamp is not a brake-system auxiliary load in the specification.

Paragraph 5.2.20.7 is a lead-in for auxiliary equipment supplied from the electric control transmission of the brake system. The rear lamp specification does not indicate that it is supplied from a brake energy reserve.

Clause 5.2.20.7.1 governs energy reserves for service braking with electric control transmission, where auxiliary equipment draws energy from that transmission. The product is a rear lamp module (rear position, stop, reversing lamps, retro-reflector) with LED modules on PCB. The spec does not say the lamp is supplied from a brake energy reservoir or electric control transmission, and the lamp is not braking equipment, so this clause does not apply.

Clause 5.2.20.7.2 concerns the parking-brake energy reservoir and lights supplied from it during a source failure. The spec describes an LED rear lamp with no brake-reservoir or electric-control-transmission supply, and the clause addresses vehicle braking-system energy rather than the lamp's own function. Not applicable to this product.

Clause 5.2.21 sets general requirements for optical brake failure and defect warning signals on the driver's indication. The rear lamp spec covers rear position, stop, reversing lamps, and reflector, not a brake-system warning signal, so the clause does not apply.

Clause 5.2.21.1 requires the vehicle to provide brake failure and defect warning signals. Those are driver-facing braking-system indicators, not functions of the rear lamp module described in the spec.

Clause 5.2.21.1.1 and 5.2.21.1.2 define red and yellow brake warning signals for braking-system failures. The rear lamp spec does not include any brake-system warning indicator, so the clause does not apply to this product.

Clause 5.2.21.1.3 requires warning signals to use the brake system malfunction symbol from UN R121. The rear lamp spec describes no brake malfunction symbol or warning signal, so the clause does not apply.
Clause 5.2.21.2 sets visibility and verifiability requirements for brake warning signals. The rear lamp spec includes no brake warning signal, so the clause does not apply.
Clause 5.2.21.3 is a lead-in to conditions for brake warning signals. The product spec has no such signal, so it does not apply.

Clause 5.2.21.3.1 requires braking-system failures to be signalled to the driver on brake actuation. The rear lamp has no braking-system failure signalling function in the spec, so the clause does not apply.

Paragraph 2.2 introduces the notion of 'different types' of headlamps and similar devices for approval purposes. It does not apply to rear lamps, which are outside the Regulation's scope.

Paragraph 2.2.2 concerns the optical system characteristics as a type-differentiation criterion for in-scope devices. It does not apply to the rear lamp, which is outside the scope.

Paragraph 2.2.6 concerns AFS front-lighting functions. The product is a rear lamp, not an AFS, so this does not apply.

Paragraph 2.2.8 is part of R149's type-definition provisions, and R149 scope (paragraph 1) covers headlamps, AFS, ADB, front fog lamps and cornering lamps. The product is a rear lamp with rear position, stop and reversing functions, so R149 does not apply to it.
Paragraph 2.3 defines 'main mode' for headlamps and AFS. The specified product has no headlamp or AFS function, and R149 scope does not include rear lamps.

decisions.reason: Heading for the photometer head description. It describes test apparatus for the laboratory, not a product feature or obligation.

Requires the test instrument (photometer head) to be spectrally corrected to the CIE photopic observer. This is a laboratory equipment requirement, not a requirement on the rear lamp's design, materials, or performance.
Concerns the local sensitivity uniformity of the measuring device's aperture and the use of diffusing windows. This applies to test equipment, not to the product.
Introductory note on best-practice measurement precautions in retro-reflection photometry. It is laboratory guidance and imposes no product obligation.
Heading for residual and stray light subsection. It contains no product obligation.
Lab precautions on matt black backgrounds, sample holders and restricted fields of view to minimise stray light. These are test-setup practices, not product requirements.
Test-room practice requiring baffles to screen floor and wall reflections during measurement. It is not a product requirement.
Describes measuring and subtracting residual stray light during testing. This is a measurement correction procedure, not a product obligation.
Heading for apparatus stability subsection. It contains no product obligation.
Requires the photometric apparatus and light source to be stable during testing and the laboratory temperature to be steady. These are test-equipment conditions, not product obligations.

Manual cleaning with n-heptane and detergent applies to a test sample of retro-reflective marking material under Annex 8 Part 1. The spec lists no marking material, so this test does not apply.

The power-washing test sits under the Part 1 heading for retro-reflective marking materials, and the spec lists no marking material or adhesive-applied sheeting. The retro-reflector is a molded PMMA prism, so this test is not triggered by the spec.

The spec's retro-reflector is a molded PMMA prism element integral to the lamp housing, not an adhesive marking material applied to a substrate.
Removability test for adhesive retro-reflective marking material. The spec describes a molded prism retro-reflector in the lamp housing, not an adhesively applied marking material.

Section heading for Part 3 (flexing of marking materials on flexible substrates such as tarpaulin). The product is a rigid rear lamp and does not use a flexible substrate.
Applies only to samples adhered to a flexible substrate such as tarpaulin. The spec describes no tarpaulin or flexible substrate.
Bend test on a 50 x 300 mm specimen of a marking material adhered to a flexible substrate. Not applicable to the rear lamp's molded retro-reflector.
Test temperature for the flexing test on flexible-substrate marking material. Not applicable to the product.
Post-flex performance criterion for flexible-substrate marking material. Not applicable to the product.

Section heading for Part 4 (resistance to impact).
