decisions.reason: Section heading for Part 5, rigidity of rear retro-reflective marking plates for HLV/SMV. The rear lamp is an M1 passenger-car lamp module, not a marking plate.

This clause sets Part 5 rigidity classes for HLV retro-reflective marking plates. The product is a rear lamp for an M1 passenger car with a retro-reflector integrated in the housing, not a separate HLV marking plate. The R150 scope (context clause 1) lists HLV plates as a separate device type, so this does not apply.
This is the plate-loading test procedure for HLV marking plates. The product has no marking plate, and the rear lamp's retro-reflector is not the device tested under this Part 5 procedure.
This is the deflection acceptance limit for HLV marking plates tested under paragraph 1.1. The product has no HLV marking plate, so the limit does not apply.
This introduces the SMV plate classes 1 and 2. The product is an M1 passenger car rear lamp with no slow-moving-vehicle marking plate, so this does not apply.
This is the SMV triangular plate holding and force test. The product has no SMV triangular plate, so this test does not apply.
This is the SMV triangular plate apex movement limit. The product has no SMV triangular plate, so the limit does not apply.
This is the SMV triangular plate residual deflection requirement. The product has no SMV triangular plate, so the requirement does not apply.
This heading introduces Advance Warning Triangle (AWT) test procedures. The product is a rear lamp, not an advance warning triangle, so this does not apply.
This heading covers the clearance-to-ground test for advance warning triangles. The product is not an advance warning triangle, so this does not apply.
This requires an advance warning triangle to pass the clearance-to-ground test. The product is a rear lamp and not an advance warning triangle, so this does not apply.
This describes the test apparatus for advance warning triangle ground clearance. The product is not an advance warning triangle, so this does not apply.
This describes the support placement procedure for the advance warning triangle ground-clearance test. The product is not an advance warning triangle, so this does not apply.

Annex 9 para 1.1.2.1 is part of the clearance-to-ground test for Advance Warning Triangles (AWT) of Type 1 and 2. The product is a rear lamp module (rear position, stop, reversing lamps, outer lens, retro-reflector), not an advance warning triangle, so this test does not apply.
Annex 9 para 1.1.2.2 sets a base-plane distance requirement for the advance warning triangle test apparatus. It concerns AWTs, which the product is not, so it does not apply to the rear lamp.
Annex 9 section 2 heading introduces the mechanical solidity test for advance warning triangles. The product is a rear lamp, not an AWT, so the test does not apply.
Annex 9 para 2.1 specifies a 2 N force applied to the apex of an advance warning triangle. The product is not an AWT, so this solidity test does not apply.
Annex 9 para 2.2 sets a 5 cm displacement limit for the apex of an advance warning triangle under the solidity test. The product is not an AWT, so it does not apply.
Annex 9 para 2.3 requires an AWT to keep its original position after the solidity test. The product is a rear lamp, not an AWT, so this requirement does not apply.
Annex 9 section 3 heading introduces the heat and low-temperature resistance test for advance warning triangles. The product is a rear lamp, not an AWT, so the test does not apply.
Annex 9 para 3.1 sets the 60 °C heat-exposure condition for an advance warning triangle in its protective cover. The product is a rear lamp, not an AWT, so this condition does not apply.

Annex 9 para 3.2 applies heat-test outcomes to an advance warning triangle, including its retro-reflective device and protective cover. The product's retro-reflector is part of a rear lamp, not an AWT, so this AWT test does not apply.
Annex 9 para 3.3 sets the cold-storage sequence for an advance warning triangle. The product is a rear lamp, not an AWT, so this test does not apply.
Annex 9 para 3.4 sets post-cold-test criteria for an advance warning triangle and its protective cover. The product is a rear lamp, not an AWT, so these criteria do not apply.
Annex 9 section 4 heading introduces the 'sandy beach' road-roughness method used for the AWT wind-stability test. The product is a rear lamp, not an AWT, and the method does not apply to it.

Annex 9 4.1 states the purpose of the sand-beach roughness method, which applies to the road surface under an advance warning triangle (AWT). The product is a rear lamp module, not an AWT, and the R150 scope (paragraph 1) covers AWT Type 1 and 2 only, so this does not apply.

Annex 9 4.1.1 concerns measuring the geometric roughness of the road surface during the AWT wind-stability test. The spec describes a rear lamp with position, stop, reversing and retro-reflector functions and no advance warning triangle, so the test does not apply.
Annex 9 4.2 gives the principle of the sand-beach roughness method for a road surface. It is a test method for AWT stability and has no link to the rear lamp's components or functions.
Annex 9 4.2.1 defines the mean sand depth calculation for the road surface. This is an AWT test-site procedure and does not apply to the rear lamp product.
Annex 9 4.2.2 specifies sand grain size, volume and disc dimensions for measuring road surface roughness in the AWT test. The rear lamp spec contains no related test equipment or obligation.
Annex 9 4.3 is the performance procedure for the sand-beach roughness test on the road surface. It is not a requirement for a rear lamp.
Annex 9 4.3.1 requires brushing the test surface before the sand test. This concerns road-surface preparation for the AWT test and does not apply to the rear lamp.
Annex 9 4.3.2 describes spreading sand on the test surface. This is part of the road-roughness measurement for AWT testing and has no bearing on the rear lamp.
Annex 9 4.3.3 covers measuring the sand patch diameters and calculating mean sand depth. This is an AWT test-site procedure and does not apply to the rear lamp.
Annex 9 4.3.4 requires six sand tests on the supporting surface to obtain the mean sand depth for the AWT. This is not applicable to a rear lamp product.
Annex 9 section 5 is the wind-stability test for advance warning triangles. The product is a rear lamp, not an AWT, so this test does not apply.
Annex 9 5.1 sets the wind-tunnel test base and surface roughness for AWT stability testing. It applies to advance warning triangles only and does not apply to the rear lamp.

Section 5.2 sets wind-tunnel air-flow conditions for testing an advance warning triangle (AWT). The product is a passenger-car rear lamp module with position, stop, reversing, and retro-reflector functions, not an AWT, so this test does not apply.
Section 5.3 requires a 3-minute open-air stream test of an advance warning triangle. The product is not an AWT, so this test does not apply.
Section 5.4 requires an advance warning triangle to resist overturning or shifting in wind. The product is not an AWT and has no such stability obligation.

Section 5.5 limits rotation of the retro-reflecting triangular part of a device during the AWT wind test. The product's retro-reflector is a rectangular lamp-integrated element, not the triangular part of an AWT, so this does not apply.

Annex 10 is an introductory note giving example approval-marking arrangements for R150 retro-reflective devices. It imposes no product obligation, and the spec does not state that the rear lamp's retro-reflector is approved under R150.

Figure A10-I shows marking examples for single R150 retro-reflective devices. The spec does not establish that the rear lamp or its retro-reflector is a separately approved R150 single device; the retro-reflector is integrated in a lamp module, so this example does not establish an obligation for this product.

Figure A10-II shows simplified marking examples for grouped or combined R150 devices. It is an example figure with no product-specific obligation, and the spec does not show an R150 approval of the rear lamp.

Figure A10-III shows the approval mark for retro-reflective marking material (conspicuity markings). The product's retro-reflector is a lamp-integrated reflector, not marking material, and the spec does not establish R150 marking-material approval.
Figure A10-IV shows the approval mark arrangement for rear marking plates and SMV devices. The product is not a rear marking plate or slow-moving vehicle device.
Figure A10-V shows the approval mark arrangement for advance warning triangles. The product is not an AWT.

Annex 11 heading for installation guidelines for rear marking plates on slow-moving vehicles and their trailers. The product is a passenger-car (M1) rear lamp, not an SMV or trailer rear marking plate.

Annex 11 paragraph 1 is a recommendation to governments to require SMV rear marking plates on vehicles that cannot exceed 30 km/h. The product is an M1 passenger-car rear lamp, outside this slow-moving vehicle scope.

Annex 11 para 2 scopes rear marking plates to slow-moving vehicles that by construction cannot exceed 30 km/h. The product is a rear lamp module for an M1 passenger car, which is not a slow-moving vehicle, and the spec lists no rear marking plate.

The number requirement (at least one rear marking plate) belongs to the slow-moving vehicle marking plate scheme. The spec describes an M1 passenger car rear lamp with position, stop, reversing lamps, outer lens and a retro-reflector, and no SMV marking plate.

Arrangement rules (apex up, within 5 degrees of transverse plane) apply to rear marking plates on slow-moving vehicles. The product's retro-reflector is an integrated lamp-housing component, not a separate rear marking plate on an SMV, so this clause does not apply.

Position rules (height 250–1,500 mm, side and rear placement) govern rear marking plates on slow-moving vehicles and their trailers. The M1 passenger car rear lamp in the spec is not such a plate, so this clause does not apply.

Geometric visibility angles (30° horizontal, 15° vertical) apply to rear marking plates on slow-moving vehicles. The spec does not include such a plate, and the lamp's retro-reflector is not assessed under this SMV annex.

The introduction describes the intent of UN R152 for Advanced Emergency Braking Systems (AEBS) on M1/N1 vehicles. The product is a rear lamp module (rear position, stop, reversing lamps, outer lens, retro-reflector), not an AEBS or braking-control system, so this background does not apply to it.

Paragraph 1 scopes approval of an on-board AEBS for collision avoidance or mitigation with passenger cars, pedestrians and bicycles. The specification describes a rear lamp with lens and retro-reflector and no collision-detection or braking system. The M1 category match does not bring the lamp within this system-level scope.
Section 2 is only a heading introducing the definitions. It creates no obligation and does not relate to a rear lamp.

Defines the Advanced Emergency Braking System as a system that detects imminent forward collisions and activates vehicle braking. The rear lamp has no collision detection or braking-activation function. The stop lamp only signals braking and does not activate it, so the definition does not cover the product.

Defines 'Emergency Braking' as a braking demand sent by the AEBS to the service brake system. The rear lamp does not emit a braking demand; its stop lamp only indicates braking. The definition does not apply.

Defines 'Collision Warning' as a warning emitted by the AEBS to the driver. The rear lamp is an external signalling device for other road users and is not an AEBS driver warning, so the definition does not apply.

Defines 'Vehicle Type with Regard to its Advanced Emergency Braking System'. It concerns vehicle features and the AEBS design, not exterior lighting components. The rear lamp specification contains no AEBS features.
Defines 'Subject Vehicle' as the vehicle being tested under R152. It is a test-procedure definition with no link to a rear lamp component.
Defines 'Soft Target' for AEBS collision tests. This is a test-target definition and does not concern the rear lamp product.
Defines 'Vehicle Target' for AEBS test scenarios. This is a test-target definition and does not concern the rear lamp product.
Defines 'Pedestrian Target' for AEBS test scenarios. This is a test-target definition and does not concern the rear lamp product.
Defines 'Bicycle Target' for AEBS test scenarios. This is a test-target definition and does not concern the rear lamp product.

Paragraph 2.10 defines "Common Space" for display information functions such as symbols. It belongs to the AEBS regulation's definitions and does not concern a rear lamp's signalling, stop, reversing, or retro-reflective functions described in the specification.

Paragraph 2.11 defines "Self-Check" as a continuous failure check of an integrated system. R152 applies to on-board AEBS, and the specification describes a passive lamp module with no electronic AEBS function.

Paragraph 2.12 defines Time To Collision for collision-avoidance calculations between the subject vehicle and a target. The rear lamp specification has no collision detection or target-tracking function.

Paragraph 2.13 defines a dry road with good adhesion in terms of peak braking coefficient and deceleration. It is a test-surface definition for AEBS performance and does not apply to a rear lamp component.

Paragraph 2.14 defines sufficient nominal peak braking coefficient values for road-friction testing. It is an AEBS test-condition definition and has no connection to the rear lamp's materials, light functions, or markings.

Paragraph 2.15 defines AEBS initialisation as the start-up process of the system after vehicle switch-on. The specification describes a passive lamp module and does not include an AEBS or any initialisation process.
Paragraph 2.16 defines the mass of a vehicle in running order for test loading. It is a vehicle-level mass definition and does not govern a rear lamp module.
Paragraph 2.17 defines maximum mass as stated by the vehicle manufacturer. It is a vehicle-level mass definition and has no bearing on the rear lamp product described.
Paragraph 2.18 defines the mean fully developed deceleration (dm) used in AEBS braking tests. It is a test-measurement definition and does not apply to a rear lamp component.

Heading 3 (Application for approval) introduces the R152 vehicle-type approval procedure for AEBS. The specification describes a rear lamp component, not an AEBS vehicle type submission, so the approval procedure does not apply to this product.

Paragraph 3.1 requires the vehicle manufacturer to apply for approval of a vehicle type with regard to AEBS. The rear lamp is a vehicle component and is not the AEBS vehicle type being approved, so this obligation does not apply to the product.
Paragraph 3.2 lists the documents to accompany an AEBS vehicle-type approval application. This is an administrative obligation for the vehicle manufacturer and is not triggered by a rear lamp module.

Paragraph 3.2.1 requires approval documentation for an AEBS (Advanced Emergency Braking System) vehicle type. Scope (para 1) covers M1/N1 vehicles with on-board collision-avoidance systems. The product is a rear lamp module (position, stop, reversing lamps, outer lens, retro-reflector), not an AEBS or a vehicle type, so this documentation obligation does not apply.
Paragraph 3.3 requires a representative vehicle to be submitted to the technical service for AEBS approval tests. The product is a rear lamp component, not a vehicle submitted for AEBS testing.
Paragraph 4 is a section heading for AEBS approval. It creates no obligation, and the product is not an AEBS approval subject.
Paragraph 4.1 grants approval of an AEBS-equipped vehicle type that meets paragraph 5. The rear lamp is not a vehicle type under R152 and does not implement the AEBS functions in paragraph 1.
Paragraph 4.2 governs approval number assignment for a vehicle type equipped with AEBS. It does not apply to a rear lamp component.

Paragraph 4.3 concerns communication of AEBS approval, refusal or withdrawal between Contracting Parties. It is an administrative obligation on approval authorities, not a product requirement for the rear lamp.

Paragraph 4.4 requires an international approval mark on every vehicle conforming to an R152-approved vehicle type. The product is a lamp module, not a vehicle conforming to an AEBS approval, so the vehicle approval mark obligation does not apply to it.
Paragraph 4.4.1 specifies the circle with the country distinguishing letter 'E' and number for the vehicle approval mark. It applies to the vehicle-level R152 approval mark, not to the rear lamp.
Paragraph 4.4.2 specifies the R152 regulation number and approval number on the vehicle approval mark. It does not apply to a rear lamp component.
Paragraph 4.5 covers how the R152 symbol and other regulation numbers are arranged when a vehicle is approved under several regulations. It concerns the vehicle approval mark, not the rear lamp.
Paragraph 4.6 requires the approval mark to be legible and indelible. It applies to the vehicle approval mark, and the rear lamp spec does not include any approval mark on the lamp.
Paragraph 4.7 requires the approval mark to be placed close to or on the vehicle data plate. This is a vehicle-level marking rule and does not apply to the rear lamp module.

Paragraph 5 is the specifications section of UN R152, which covers an on-board Advanced Emergency Braking System (AEBS) for M1/N1 vehicles. The product is a rear lamp module (position, stop, reversing lamps, lens, retro-reflector), not an AEBS or a vehicle system, so the scope does not match.
5.1 sets general AEBS performance requirements. The product is a rear lamp and has no collision-avoidance function, sensors, or braking control, so the clause does not apply.

5.1.1 applies to vehicles fitted with an AEBS. The rear lamp specification describes no AEBS, so the condition is not met. The paragraph is also flagged as an ambiguous numbered line, but that does not change the outcome.
5.1.1.4 is an AEBS performance cross-reference for car-to-bicycle scenarios. The product is a rear lamp with no AEBS, so it does not apply.
5.1.2 concerns the immunity of AEBS to magnetic and electrical fields. The rear lamp spec contains no AEBS electronics or sensing function, so it does not apply.

5.1.3 requires electronic control system safety for the AEBS under Annex 3. The product spec describes passive lamp electronics only (LED modules on PCB) with no AEBS control system, so it does not apply.
5.1.4 requires the AEBS to give the driver collision and status warnings. The rear lamp has no driver warning function tied to an AEBS, so it does not apply.
5.1.4.1 requires a failure warning for the AEBS. The rear lamp spec describes no AEBS and no failure warning for such a system, so it does not apply.
5.1.4.1.1 concerns AEBS self-check timing and warning illumination for electrically detectable failures. The rear lamp is not an AEBS, so it does not apply.
5.1.4.1.2 concerns AEBS detection of non-electrical failures such as sensor blindness or misalignment. The rear lamp has no sensors in its spec, so it does not apply.
5.1.4.2 concerns AEBS initialisation status indication after driving time above 10 km/h. The rear lamp spec describes no AEBS, so it does not apply.
5.1.4.3 requires a deactivation warning for an AEBS that has a deactivation means. The rear lamp spec describes no AEBS and no deactivation means, so it does not apply.

Clause 5.1.5 sets emergency braking performance for an Advanced Emergency Braking System (AEBS) fitted to a vehicle. The spec describes a rear lamp module with position, stop, reversing lamps, outer lens and retro-reflector, and no AEBS, sensing, or braking-control function. The clause does not apply to this lamp.
Clause 5.1.6 concerns AEBS false-reaction avoidance and collision-warning logic. The rear lamp has no collision warning or automatic braking function, so the clause does not apply.

Clause 5.1.7 requires an AEBS-equipped vehicle to meet UN R13-H or R13 performance and to have an anti-lock braking function. The spec describes a lamp module, not a vehicle AEBS or ABS, so the clause does not apply to this product.
Clause 5.2 is a heading for AEBS specific requirements. It imposes no obligation, and the rear lamp is not an AEBS.
Clause 5.2.1 is a heading for the car-to-car AEBS scenario. It imposes no obligation, and the rear lamp has no collision-avoidance function.

Clause 5.2.1.1 sets collision-warning timing for a vehicle AEBS detecting a preceding vehicle. The rear lamp has no radar or sensing and issues no collision warning, so the clause does not apply. The stop lamp's signalling to following drivers is a lighting function governed by other regulations, not this AEBS warning requirement.
Clause 5.2.1.2 requires an AEBS to demand at least 5.0 m/s² of braking when a collision is imminent. The rear lamp does not demand vehicle braking, so the clause does not apply.
Clause 5.2.1.3 sets the vehicle speed range over which an AEBS must be active. The rear lamp has no speed-dependent active function, so the clause does not apply.

Clause 5.2.1.4 sets maximum relative impact speed tables for an AEBS under specified conditions. It relates to vehicle braking performance and the rear lamp has no such function, so the clause does not apply.
Clause 5.2.2 is a heading for the car-to-pedestrian AEBS scenario. It imposes no obligation, and the rear lamp is not an AEBS.
Clause 5.2.2.1 sets pedestrian collision-warning requirements for an AEBS. The rear lamp has no pedestrian detection or warning function, so the clause does not apply.
Clause 5.2.2.2 requires an AEBS to demand at least 5.0 m/s² of braking for a pedestrian collision. The rear lamp does not demand vehicle braking, so the clause does not apply.

Clause 5.2.2.3 sets the active speed range for the AEBS car-to-pedestrian function on M1/N1 vehicles. The product is a rear lamp module (position, stop, reversing lamps, retro-reflector, outer lens), not an on-board AEBS or vehicle system, so this clause does not apply to it.

Clause 5.2.2.4 covers the AEBS speed-reduction performance (impact speed tables for pedestrian scenarios) for vehicles. The rear lamp spec does not include any braking-control or sensing system. Its stop lamp only signals braking and does not perform the AEBS impact-speed function, so the clause does not apply.
Heading 5.2.3 introduces the car-to-bicycle AEBS scenario. It is a section heading with no obligation, and it concerns a vehicle system that the rear lamp module does not implement.

Clause 5.2.3.1 requires an AEBS collision warning for a bicycle scenario. The rear lamp spec describes no warning, detection, or driver-alert function for collisions. The product is a lamp, so the clause does not apply.

Clause 5.2.3.2 requires a minimum 5.0 m/s² braking demand to the service brakes during AEBS emergency braking. The rear lamp spec does not include braking control, deceleration demand, or an AEBS function. The stop lamp is only a signalling output and does not satisfy or relate to this braking-demand obligation.
Clause 5.2.3.3 sets the active speed range for the AEBS bicycle function. The product is a rear lamp module, not an AEBS system, so the clause does not apply.

Clause 5.2.3.4 sets AEBS speed-reduction impact-speed limits for cyclist scenarios on vehicles. The rear lamp spec contains no AEBS, braking control, or sensing function, so the clause does not apply.
Heading 5.3 introduces driver interruption of AEBS. It is a section heading with no obligation, and the rear lamp spec describes no AEBS driver-interface function.

Clause 5.3.1 requires the AEBS to provide the driver a means to interrupt collision warning and emergency braking. The rear lamp spec has no driver-interruption or AEBS control function, so the clause does not apply.

Clause 5.3.2 covers positive driver actions that interrupt AEBS and the manufacturer's list of those actions. The rear lamp spec describes no AEBS interruption logic, so the clause does not apply to this product.
Heading 5.4 introduces AEBS deactivation. It is a section heading with no obligation, and the rear lamp spec describes no manual AEBS deactivation means.
Clause 5.4.1 sets conditions for a manual AEBS deactivation switch on vehicles. The rear lamp spec has no AEBS function or deactivation means, so the clause does not apply.

Paragraph 5.4.1.1 concerns automatic reinstatement of the AEBS (advanced emergency braking system) at powertrain initiation. R152 applies to vehicle-level collision-avoidance systems, and the rear lamp specification describes only a lighting module with position, stop, reversing lamps, lens and retro-reflector. Nothing in the spec relates to AEBS.
This footnote defines propulsion-system terminology for the AEBS context of R152. It creates no obligation for a rear lamp and has no product link.
Paragraph 5.4.1.2 governs how many deliberate actions are needed to manually deactivate the AEBS control. The rear lamp spec contains no driver control or AEBS function.
Paragraph 5.4.1.3 requires the AEBS control to be installed per UN R121. That is a driver-control and warning-installation rule for the vehicle, not a requirement for a rear lamp module.
Paragraph 5.4.1.4 restricts manual deactivation of the AEBS above 10 km/h. This concerns the AEBS system and does not apply to the rear lamp.
Paragraph 5.4.2 sets conditions for automatic AEBS deactivation (off-road use, towing, dynamometer, washing). It applies to the AEBS function, not to the rear lamp specified here.

Paragraph 5.4.2.1 requires the manufacturer to list AEBS automatic deactivation situations for the type-approval test report. This is a documentation duty for the AEBS system and does not involve the rear lamp.
Paragraph 5.4.2.2 requires automatic reactivation of the AEBS function once deactivation conditions cease. This concerns the AEBS function, not the rear lamp.
Paragraph 5.4.2.3 requires two deliberate driver actions to deactivate AEBS when the ESC is switched off. The rear lamp spec contains no ESC or AEBS interface.

Paragraph 5.4.3 requires a constant optical warning when AEBS is deactivated, and it allows the yellow warning in 5.5.4. The yellow warning is a dashboard indicator for AEBS, not the rear stop, position or reversing lamps. The rear lamp spec does not include a driver warning indicator.
Paragraph 5.4.4 allows AEBS suspension while automated driving functions control longitudinal motion. It concerns vehicle automated-driving and AEBS logic and does not apply to the rear lamp module.
Paragraph 5.5 is a heading for the AEBS warning indication requirements. It creates no obligation, and the rear lamp spec contains no AEBS warning function.

Paragraph 5.5.1 governs the AEBS collision warning (acoustic, haptic or optical modes) under UN R152, whose scope (context clause 1) is on-board AEBS systems on M1/N1 vehicles. The product is a rear lamp module with position, stop, reversing and retro-reflector functions, not an AEBS or its driver warning, so the clause does not apply.
Paragraph 5.5.2 requires the manufacturer to describe the AEBS warning indication and sequence. This concerns the AEBS driver-warning system, not the rear lamp product in the specification.

Paragraph 5.3.3 governs when an ALKS emergency manoeuvre may be terminated. R157 applies to ALKS vehicle-control systems of M and N1 vehicles. The rear lamp spec describes only position, stop, reversing, and retro-reflector lighting functions, with no automated driving or emergency manoeuvre function.

Paragraph 5.3.3.1 requires an ALKS to keep operating after an emergency manoeuvre. The rear lamp spec describes no driving-automation function, so this system-behaviour obligation does not apply to the lamp module.

Paragraph 5.3.3.2 requires the ALKS to generate hazard-warning activation and deactivation signals after a standstill emergency manoeuvre. Paragraph 5.3.4 requires the vehicle to implement a logic signal indicating emergency braking per UN R13-H or R13. This is a vehicle ALKS signal obligation. The rear lamp spec includes a stop lamp, but it does not say the module generates the emergency-braking logic signal, so the obligation does not attach to this product.
Paragraph 5.3.5 is a heading for ALKS evasive lane crossing and contains no standalone obligation. The rear lamp spec describes no lane-keeping or evasive-manoeuvre function.
Paragraph 5.3.5.1 requires an ALKS to aim to avoid an evasive lane crossing. This is an automated driving behaviour. The rear lamp spec describes only lighting functions and no ALKS.
Paragraph 5.3.5.2 sets the safety standard for an ALKS evasive lane crossing. It applies to automated vehicle control, not to a rear lamp module.
Paragraph 5.3.5.3 requires the ALKS to have sufficient surrounding-environment information before crossing lane markings. The rear lamp spec includes no sensing or perception function.
Paragraph 5.3.5.4 prohibits an ALKS evasive lane crossing from causing a collision. This is an automated driving obligation and does not apply to the rear lamp spec.
Paragraph 5.3.5.5 governs unmanageable deceleration of other vehicles caused by an ALKS evasive manoeuvre. The rear lamp spec describes no automated driving function.
Paragraph 5.3.5.6 requires the ALKS to aim to return to its original lane after an evasive crossing. This is an automated driving behaviour outside the rear lamp scope.

Paragraph 5.3.5.7 requires an ALKS evasive lane crossing to be indicated by generating the direction-indicator activation signal. The rear lamp spec includes no direction indicator function, and this signal is generated by the ALKS, not by the rear lamp module.

Requires the ALKS to recognise situations needing transition of control to the driver. The rear lamp has no driving-control or ALKS function, so this obligation does not apply to the product.
Concerns timing of transition demands for a safe handover to manual driving by an ALKS. The rear lamp product has no ALKS and no driver-handover function.

Covers ALKS failure detection and immediate transition demand. The rear lamp is not an ALKS and its lighting functions are not governed by this clause.

Requires the vehicle to generate a hazard warning signal within 5 s once at standstill during an ALKS transition. The rear lamp specification does not include hazard-signal control logic or ALKS-driven signalling, so this clause does not apply to the lamp module.
Requires escalation of a transition demand within 4 s. This is an ALKS human-machine interaction requirement and does not apply to the rear lamp.

Requires a minimum risk manoeuvre if the driver does not respond to a transition demand. This is an ALKS control requirement and does not apply to the passive rear lamp module.

Paragraph 5.4.4.1.2 requires the manufacturer to declare ALKS failure types that trigger a minimum risk manoeuvre. The specification describes no ALKS, so this declaration obligation does not apply to the rear lamp.

Paragraph 5.5.1 defines how an ALKS minimum risk manoeuvre brings the vehicle to standstill. The rear lamp specification contains no vehicle motion control or ALKS function.

Paragraph 5.5.2 sets an ALKS deceleration demand and hazard-light activation during a minimum risk manoeuvre. The specified rear lamp has no ALKS, deceleration control, or hazard signal generation logic. Its stop lamp is a braking indicator only, not an ALKS function.
Paragraph 5.5.3 concerns termination of an ALKS minimum risk manoeuvre. The rear lamp has no such control logic.
Paragraph 5.5.4 requires the ALKS to deactivate at the end of a minimum risk manoeuvre and keeps hazard lights active. The rear lamp specification does not describe an ALKS or hazard control logic.
Paragraph 5.5.5 governs ALKS reactivation after a minimum risk manoeuvre, tied to powertrain initiation. The rear lamp has no ALKS or powertrain control function.

Paragraph 6.2.2 sets the default off-mode of an ALKS at powertrain initiation. The rear lamp is not an ALKS, so this does not apply.

Paragraph 6.2.4 covers manual deactivation of an ALKS by the driver. The rear lamp spec has no ALKS, so this does not apply.
Paragraph 6.2.5 restricts ALKS deactivation by driver inputs. The rear lamp has no ALKS, so this does not apply.
Paragraph 6.2.5.1 covers ALKS deactivation through steering, braking or acceleration inputs. The rear lamp spec describes no driving controls or ALKS, so this does not apply.
Paragraph 6.2.5.2 covers ALKS deactivation during a transition demand or minimum risk manoeuvre. The rear lamp is not an ALKS and performs no such manoeuvre, so this does not apply.
Paragraph 6.2.5.3 covers ALKS deactivation delay during an emergency manoeuvre. The rear lamp has no ALKS or emergency manoeuvre function, so this does not apply.

Paragraph 6.2.7 requires indicating ALKS deactivation to the driver under 6.4.2.3. The product is a rear lamp with no ALKS and no driver-information function for automated deactivation.

Paragraph 6.3.6 allows the ALKS to reduce driver-input effects during imminent collisions. The product is a rear lamp with no collision-avoidance or control function.
Paragraph 6.3.7 covers ALKS override strategies in severe vehicle or ALKS failures. The rear lamp spec describes no ALKS, override, or failure strategy.

Paragraph 6.4.2 is a heading for ALKS system-status display. The rear lamp has no ALKS system status to display.

Paragraph 6.4.4 allows alternative optical-signal interface designs for ALKS HMI examples, assessed by the Technical Service. It applies only to ALKS HMI displays, which the rear lamp does not have.

7.1.2 covers the declared lateral detection range of an ALKS sensing system. The rear lamp has no sensing function and the spec mentions no ALKS.

Paragraph 8.4.3.3 concerns retrieval of DSSAD data when the main vehicle power supply is unavailable. The rear lamp specification describes no data recorder or power-supply retrieval function.

decisions.reason: Paragraph 3.3 requires submitting a vehicle representative of the type to the approval authority for DCAS approval tests. The product is a rear lamp module, not a DCAS-equipped vehicle or a vehicle type under R171. R171 scope (1.1) covers only DCAS in M and N2 vehicles.

Paragraph 5.1.2 covers DCAS mode awareness and avoidance of driver overreliance. The rear lamp product has no DCAS mode or driver-interaction function, so this does not apply.

Paragraph 5.1.3 covers guarding a DCAS against misuse and unauthorised modification of its software and hardware. The rear lamp specification lists no DCAS software or hardware, so this does not apply.

Paragraph 5.1.4 sets driver override/deactivation requirements for a DCAS (driver control assistance) system. The product is a passive rear lamp module (position, stop, reversing lamps, retro-reflector) with no driver-assistance function.
Paragraph 5.1.5 requires a DCAS-equipped vehicle to carry AEBS and lane departure systems. The product is a rear lamp component, not a DCAS-equipped vehicle or an AEBS/LDW/LKA system.

Paragraph 5.2.1 concerns DCAS active-mode interaction with AEBS longitudinal functionality. The rear lamp spec has no DCAS or AEBS function.
Paragraph 5.2.2 concerns transitions and prioritisation between DCAS and other assistance or automation systems, documented for the approval authority. The rear lamp spec describes no such system.

Paragraph 5.3.1 requires documentation of DCAS detection capabilities. The rear lamp has no detection or sensing function.

Paragraph 5.3.2.1 requires DCAS behaviour that avoids disrupting traffic flow. The rear lamp has no traffic-adaptive behaviour.

Paragraph 5.3.2.3 requires the DCAS to control longitudinal and lateral vehicle motion. The rear lamp has no motion-control function.

Paragraph 5.3.3 lets a DCAS activate vehicle systems such as direction indicators, wipers and heating. The rear lamp is a passive lighting module that does not activate vehicle systems, so the clause does not apply to it.

Paragraph 5.3.4 sets control-strategy requirements for a DCAS (driver control assistance system). The product is a passive rear lamp module (rear position, stop, reversing lamps, lens, retro-reflector) with no control strategy or driver assistance function, so the clause does not apply.
Heading for DCAS system-boundary response requirements. The rear lamp specification describes no DCAS or driver assistance features, so no system boundary applies.
Requires DCAS features to detect system boundaries and transition to stand-by mode. The rear lamp has no DCAS feature or mode logic, so the clause does not apply.
Concerns avoiding rapid fluctuations between DCAS 'stand-by' and 'active' modes. The rear lamp specification contains no such modes or system.
Requires manufacturer documentation of DCAS system boundary conditions. The rear lamp is not a DCAS and has no boundary conditions in its specification.
Refers to DCAS boundary-condition descriptions in Annex 3, Appendix 3. The rear lamp has no DCAS, so this does not apply.

Requires the manufacturer to identify DCAS-detectable system boundaries. The rear lamp has no detection or boundary function.
Requires justification of undetectable DCAS system boundaries. The rear lamp has no DCAS, so the clause does not apply.

Heading for DCAS controllability requirements. The rear lamp has no control actions to make controllable, so the clause does not apply.

Paragraph 5.3.7 is a heading for DCAS system dynamic control. It creates no obligation, and the rear lamp product has no dynamic vehicle control function.
Paragraph 5.3.7.1 is a heading for positioning the vehicle in its lane under DCAS. The rear lamp does not perform lane positioning, so the clause does not apply.
Paragraph 5.3.7.1.1 requires a DCAS in 'active' mode to keep the vehicle within its lane. The rear lamp spec has no steering or lane-keeping function, so this clause does not apply.

Paragraph 5.3.7.1.3 requires the DCAS lane-positioning speed and lateral-acceleration strategy to be documented and assessed. The rear lamp spec has no such strategy, so this clause does not apply.

Paragraph 5.3.7.2.3.3 concerns DCAS behaviour when a driver does not confirm a manoeuvre. The rear lamp has no such logic.

Paragraph 5.3.7.2.4.3 requires the safety concept to describe system behaviour when the driver is disengaged during a manoeuvre. The rear lamp has no driver-disengagement or safety-concept function, so it does not apply.

Paragraph 5.3.7.2.5.2 concerns following-distance readjustment by a DCAS vehicle. The rear lamp has no longitudinal control function.

decisions.reason: Paragraph 5.5.4.1.7 sets HMI distinguishability requirements for a DCAS/ADS system's status indication. Heading for the system messages and signals for driver-confirmed manoeuvres. It concerns DCAS driver HMI, not a rear lamp. The product has no messaging function and is outside R171 scope.

Requires visual driver information about proposed manoeuvres from a DCAS. The rear lamp spec describes only rear position, stop, reversing, and retro-reflector functions. It is not a driver-assistance system and falls outside the R171 scope in 1.1.
States that direction indicators do not satisfy the DCAS manoeuvre-information requirement. The rear lamp's stop and reversing lamps are not DCAS HMI signals, and the product is outside R171 scope.
Requires DCAS signals and messages to avoid driver overreliance. This is a driver-assistance HMI obligation. The rear lamp has no such system and is outside R171 scope.
Heading for system-initiated manoeuvre messages in DCAS. The product is a rear lamp with no system-initiated manoeuvre function, so the clause does not apply.
Cross-references 5.5.4.1.8 for system-initiated manoeuvre messages in DCAS. The rear lamp has no such system, so the clause does not apply.
Requires DCAS to announce upcoming manoeuvres with sufficient notice. The rear lamp spec does not describe any vehicle control or manoeuvre function, and R171 scope does not cover the product.

Requires the system to indicate whether manoeuvres can be initiated automatically. This applies only to a DCAS capable of system-initiated manoeuvres. The rear lamp has no such capability, so the clause does not apply.

Requires driver state monitoring and warning strategies for a DCAS to be documented and demonstrated to the approval authority. The rear lamp has no driver monitoring function, and R171 does not apply to this product.
Requires driver disengagement detection in a DCAS. The rear lamp has no driver-monitoring or control function, so the clause does not apply.
Requires the system to monitor motoric and visual driver disengagement. This is a DCAS driver-monitoring obligation. The rear lamp has no such function and is outside R171 scope.

Clause 5.5.4.2.1.2 concerns DCAS driver-disengagement monitoring and lane-keeping behaviour when the driver monitoring determination is unavailable. UN R171 applies to DCAS in M and N2 vehicles, and the rear lamp specification describes only signalling, stop, reversing and retro-reflective functions with no driver monitoring or lateral control.
Heading for the DCAS driver disengagement warning requirements. It concerns the HMI of a driver-assistance system, which the rear lamp does not include.
Clause 5.5.4.2.2.1 requires a DCAS warning to guide the driver. The rear lamp has no warning function or driver interface, so the clause does not apply.
Clause 5.5.4.2.2.3 concerns prioritising DCAS warnings against simultaneously active emergency assistance systems such as AEBS. The rear lamp specification has no such system.
Heading for the types of DCAS driver warnings (HOR, EOR, DCA). It is not an obligation and the rear lamp has no warning function.
Heading for the Hands On Request warning type of a DCAS. The rear lamp has no driver-warning function.

Clause 5.5.4.2.3.1.2 defines confirmation of a Hands On Request by the driver. This is a DCAS driver-interaction requirement, not applicable to a rear lamp.

Clause 5.5.4.2.3.2.1 requires a continual visual warning combined with another modality for DCAS. The rear lamp's visual signals are vehicle lighting functions, not DCAS driver warnings, so the clause does not apply.
Clause 5.5.4.2.3.2.2 defines confirmation of an Eyes On Request by the driver's visual attention. This is a DCAS driver-monitoring requirement and does not apply to the rear lamp.
Heading for the Direct Control Alert warning type of a DCAS. The rear lamp has no driver-warning function.

Paragraph 5.5.4.2.5 is a heading for the assessment of visual disengagement by a DCAS driver-state monitoring system. The rear lamp specification contains no driver-facing monitoring system, so this clause does not apply.

Paragraph 5.5.4.2.5.2 defines visual disengagement from driving-task-relevant areas for DCAS driver monitoring. The rear lamp has no driver monitoring or driving-task function.

Clause 7.1.3 concerns starting sampling pumps and switching valves in the UN R40 emissions test. The rear lamp spec has no such equipment.
Clause 7.1.4 concerns the temperature sensing device and pressure gauges in the UN R40 emissions sampling set-up. This is not applicable to a rear lamp module.
Clause 7.1.5 concerns zeroing the pump and roller revolution counters in the UN R40 emissions test. This is not applicable to the rear lamp product.

Heading for the end-of-sampling and volumetric measurement operations of the UN R40 Annex 4 emission test. This concerns L3-L5 engine exhaust sampling, which does not cover the M1 passenger-car rear lamp described in the specification.

Annex 4 emission test sequencing requirement for the end of the fourth test cycle. It applies to the UN R40 motorcycle emission test and has no connection to the rear lamp product's lighting or signalling functions.

Annex 4 emission sampling step (switching valves to discharge samples from pumps P2 and P3). This is part of the UN R40 exhaust gas sampling for L3-L5 vehicles and is not applicable to a rear lamp module.
Annex 4 emission test step marking the end of the test on analogue recorders. It belongs to the UN R40 L3-L5 exhaust emission procedure and does not relate to the passenger-car rear lamp.
Annex 4 emission test step disengaging the cumulative revolution counter from pump P1. This is part of the UN R40 motorcycle emission test and is not applicable to the rear lamp product.
Annex 4 emission test step switching off the blower. This belongs to the UN R40 exhaust emission test for L3-L5 vehicles and does not apply to the M1 rear lamp module.

Annex 4 procedure for measuring distance covered using a roller and cumulative counter. This is part of the UN R40 emission test for L3-L5 vehicles and is unrelated to the rear lamp product.
Heading for determining the quantity of gas emitted under the UN R40 Annex 4 Type-I test. It concerns L3-L5 exhaust emissions and does not cover the M1 passenger-car rear lamp module.

The spec describes a rear lamp module for an M1 passenger car with no engine or exhaust, so the clause does not apply.

Defines distance S and the CO density constant for the emissions calculation. This is an exhaust-emissions test parameter with no link to a rear lamp product, and R40 scope is L3-L5 engines.
Defines the volumetric CO concentration used in the emissions calculation. It concerns exhaust gas measurement for L3-L5 positive-ignition engines, not a lighting product.
Defines the CO concentration in the diluted-gas bag sample. This is an exhaust-sampling parameter that does not apply to a rear lamp module.
Defines the CO concentration in the diluent-air bag sample. This is an emissions-test parameter outside the spec's lighting function and outside R40's L3-L5 engine scope.
Defines the dilution coefficient DF for the emissions calculation. It is an exhaust-test parameter and does not relate to the rear lamp product.
Defines the total diluted gas volume for the emissions test. It applies to exhaust measurement of L3-L5 vehicles, not to a passenger-car rear lamp.
Defines the pump displacement volume used in the emissions dilution system. It is a test-equipment parameter with no connection to the rear lamp product.
Defines the pump revolution count for the four test cycles of the emissions test. It is not related to lighting or to the spec's product functions.
Defines the ambient pressure used in the emissions volume calculation. It is an exhaust-test parameter and does not apply to a rear lamp.
Defines the average under-pressure in the pump intake during the emissions test. It is an exhaust-test parameter and does not apply to a rear lamp.

Annex 4 / 8.2.2 defines S, the test distance, and 8.2.3 defines the hydrocarbon density used in emission calculations. Both sit inside the UN R40 L-category exhaust-emission test, which is outside the scope of a rear lamp product.

Annex 4 / 8.2.4 defines HCC, the corrected hydrocarbon concentration in diluted exhaust gas. This is part of the UN R40 exhaust-emission measurement for L3–L5 vehicles, which does not include the rear lamp product.

Annex 4 / 8.2.4.1 defines HCe, the hydrocarbon concentration in the diluted-gas sample from bag SA. This is an exhaust-sampling parameter of the UN R40 emission test, with no link to the rear lamp's lighting, signalling, or retro-reflective functions.

Annex 4 / 8.2.4.2 defines HCd, the hydrocarbon concentration in the diluent-air sample from bag SB. This is an exhaust-emission test parameter under UN R40 and does not apply to the rear lamp product.
Annex 4 / 8.2.4.3 defines the dilution coefficient DF used in exhaust-emission calculations. It is part of the UN R40 L-category Type-I test and has no application to a passenger-car rear lamp.
Annex 4 / 8.2.5 defines V, the total diluted-gas volume for the emission test. It is an exhaust-emission calculation parameter under UN R40 and does not apply to the rear lamp product.

Annex 4 / 8.3 gives the formula for nitrogen oxide mass from vehicle exhaust. It is part of the UN R40 emission calculation for L-category positive-ignition engines, which the rear lamp spec does not involve.
Annex 4 / 8.3.1 defines NOxM, the nitrogen oxide mass emitted during the test. This is an UN R40 exhaust-emission quantity for L3–L5 vehicles and has no relation to the rear lamp product.

Annex 4 / 8.3.2 and 8.3.3 define the test distance S and the nitrogen oxide density used in emission calculations. These are UN R40 exhaust-emission parameters for L-category engines and do not apply to a passenger-car rear lamp.

Annex 4 para 8.3.4 defines NOx concentration for the Type-I emissions calculation. UN R40 scope (para 1) covers gaseous pollutants from positive-ignition engines of L3, L4 and L5 vehicles. The product is a rear lamp module for an M1 passenger car, so this emissions clause does not apply.
Annex 4 para 8.3.4.1 defines NOxe for the Type-I emissions calculation. UN R40 applies to L3-L5 motorcycle engines, and the product is an M1 passenger car rear lamp, so it is out of scope.
Annex 4 para 8.3.4.2 defines NOxd for the Type-I emissions calculation. UN R40 applies to L3-L5 motorcycle engines, and the product is an M1 passenger car rear lamp, so it is out of scope.
Annex 4 para 8.3.5 defines the humidity correction factor Kh for emissions testing. UN R40 scope covers L3-L5 motorcycle engines; the product is an M1 passenger car rear lamp, so this does not apply.
Annex 4 para 8.3.5.1 defines absolute humidity H for emissions testing. UN R40 scope covers L3-L5 motorcycle engines; the product is an M1 passenger car rear lamp, so this does not apply.
Annex 4 para 8.3.5.1.1 defines percentage humidity U for emissions testing. UN R40 scope covers L3-L5 motorcycle engines; the product is an M1 passenger car rear lamp, so this does not apply.
Annex 4 para 8.3.5.1.2 defines saturated water pressure Pd for emissions testing. UN R40 scope covers L3-L5 motorcycle engines; the product is an M1 passenger car rear lamp, so this does not apply.
Annex 4 para 8.3.5.1.3 defines atmospheric pressure Pa for emissions testing. UN R40 scope covers L3-L5 motorcycle engines; the product is an M1 passenger car rear lamp, so this does not apply.
Annex 4 para 8.4 defines the DF coefficient for emissions calculations. UN R40 scope covers L3-L5 motorcycle engines; the product is an M1 passenger car rear lamp, so this does not apply.

Annex 5 heading for the Type-II idling CO emissions test. UN R40 scope covers L3-L5 motorcycle engines; the product is an M1 passenger car rear lamp, so this does not apply.

Specifies the reference fuel for the type-II exhaust emission test. The UN R40 scope (L3–L5 positive-ignition engines) does not cover a rear lamp module, which has no fuel system.
Sets the CO measurement timing at idle for the type-II test. The product is a rear lamp with no engine, and UN R40 scope does not cover M1 passenger cars.
Gearbox-position condition for the manual-gearbox type-II emission test. The product has no gearbox, and the regulation scope is L3–L5 motorcycles.
Gear-selector condition for the automatic-gearbox type-II emission test. The product has no gearbox, and the regulation scope is L3–L5 motorcycles.
Heading for the exhaust gas sampling procedure. The product has no exhaust system, and the regulation scope is L3–L5 positive-ignition engines.
Requires an air-tight exhaust extension for the sample probe. The product has no exhaust outlet, and the regulation scope does not cover it.
Concerns the determination of CO and CO2 concentrations from instrument readings. The product has no engine exhaust, and the regulation scope does not cover it.
Corrected-CO formula for two-stroke engines. The product has no engine, and the regulation scope does not cover it.
Corrected-CO formula for four-stroke engines. The product has no engine, and the regulation scope does not cover it.
States when CO concentration need not be corrected, based on the engine-type totals. The product has no engine, and the regulation scope does not cover it.
Annex 6 heading for reference fuel specifications. The product has no fuel-based engine, and the UN R40 scope (L3–L5 positive-ignition engines) does not apply to a rear lamp.

This is Annex 6, paragraph 1, which specifies reference fuels for testing positive-ignition engines under UN R40. UN R40 scope (context clause UN_R40_base:1) covers gaseous pollutant emissions from L3, L4 and L5 motorcycle categories. The product is a rear lamp module for an M1 passenger car, with no engine, fuel, or emissions function, so the clause does not apply.

This is the introduction to Annex 7, which describes a dynamometric brake method for measuring power absorbed on the road for motorcycles under UN R40. The product is a rear lamp with no dynamometer, powertrain, or road-power measurement function, and R40 scope is limited to L3–L5 vehicles, so the clause does not apply.
Annex 7, paragraph 1, is a dynamometer test step (measuring roller rotational speed) under UN R40 for motorcycles. It has no connection to a rear lamp module for an M1 passenger car.
Annex 7, paragraph 2, is a dynamometer start-up step for motorcycle emissions/power testing under UN R40. It does not apply to a rear lamp module.
Annex 7, paragraph 3, concerns inertia simulation for a dynamometer used in motorcycle testing under UN R40. It does not apply to a rear lamp module.
Annex 7, paragraph 4, sets a dynamometer speed for motorcycle road-power testing under UN R40. It does not apply to a rear lamp module.
Annex 7, paragraph 5, is a dynamometer power-reading step under UN R40 for motorcycles. It does not apply to a rear lamp module.
Annex 7, paragraph 6, is a dynamometer speed step under UN R40 for motorcycles. It does not apply to a rear lamp module.
Annex 7, paragraph 7, disconnects the dynamometer start-up device in a UN R40 motorcycle power test. It does not apply to a rear lamp module.
Annex 7, paragraph 8, is a dynamometer coast-down timing step under UN R40 for motorcycles. It does not apply to a rear lamp module.
Annex 7, paragraph 9, sets the power-absorption device level in a UN R40 motorcycle dynamometer test. It does not apply to a rear lamp module.
Annex 7, paragraph 10, repeats dynamometer test phases under UN R40 for motorcycles. It does not apply to a rear lamp module.

Annex 7 item 11 is part of the road power-absorption method for motorcycle dynamometer brakes, which is the subject of UN R40. UN R40 covers gaseous pollutant emissions from positive-ignition engines of L3, L4 and L5 vehicles (Scope, clause 1). Annex 7 item 12 concerns plotting the power absorbed by a motorcycle dynamometer against the power at 50 km/h in phase 4. It belongs to the same UN R40 motorcycle emissions test method and does not relate to the M1 rear lamp's photometric, mechanical, or signalling functions.
This is a document header and version note for UN R42 with no product obligation. It does not describe any requirement for a rear lamp.

Scope covers M1 vehicles with regard to the behaviour of front and rear protective devices in low-speed collisions. The product is a rear lamp module (position, stop, reversing lamps, lens, retro-reflector), not a protective device or a vehicle, so the scope does not match.
This is a section heading for the purpose clause and contains no obligation. The regulation's purpose concerns protective devices, which the rear lamp is not.

Describes exterior protection by protective devices (contact and small-shock resistance at vehicle ends). The specification describes a lamp module with lighting functions and a retro-reflector, not a protective device, so this does not apply.
This is a section heading for the definitions and contains no obligation.
Introductory lead-in to the definitions list. It creates no obligation and does not concern lamps.

Defines vehicle approval for the behaviour of front and rear structure in low-speed collisions. It concerns vehicle-level structural approval, not a rear lamp component's lighting or signalling function.

Defines vehicle type by structural and mass-related characteristics for the impact test. It does not apply to a rear lamp module as a product, although the lamp is a rear-structure part that could in principle affect a vehicle type; the impact-test relevance is not triggered by this spec.
Defines unladen weight of a vehicle. It is a vehicle mass definition with no bearing on a rear lamp product.
Defines laden test weight for vehicle impact testing. It has no bearing on a rear lamp product.
Defines vehicle corner for the impact test geometry. It does not concern a rear lamp product.
Defines the reference height for protective devices on the vehicle, tied to the impactor reference line. It does not apply to a rear lamp module.

Definition of 'reference line' for the bumper impactor in the low-speed collision test. R42 covers the behaviour of front and rear protective devices (bumpers) of M1 vehicles. Heading for the approval application section of R42, which concerns vehicle-type approval of bumper protection in low-speed collisions. The rear lamp specification does not describe a bumper or vehicle-type bumper approval, so the section does not apply to this product.

Requires the vehicle manufacturer to apply for approval of a vehicle type for bumper protection in low-speed collisions. The product is a rear lamp module, not a vehicle type or bumper system, so this application obligation does not apply to the product.

Lists application documents for bumper and protective-device approval (structure, dimensions, constituent materials, protective device description). The rear lamp is not a protective device. Its outer lens and housing materials do not bring it under this bumper documentation requirement.

Requires a representative vehicle to be submitted to a technical service for bumper low-speed collision tests. The product is a rear lamp component, not a vehicle submitted for these tests, so the clause does not apply.

Concerns accepting a vehicle with omitted components for the bumper collision test. It relates to vehicle test configuration for protective devices, not to the rear lamp product, which is not a test vehicle or a bumper component.

Places a responsibility on the applicant to show that variants are compatible with R42 bumper requirements. This is an approval-administration obligation for vehicle types and does not apply to the rear lamp module.
Section heading for approval of a vehicle type under R42 bumper requirements. It creates no obligation for the rear lamp product.

Grants approval of a vehicle type when it meets the R42 bumper low-speed collision requirements in paragraph 6. The rear lamp is not a vehicle type, and the clause is not a lighting requirement for the lamp.
Specifies how approval numbers are assigned to vehicle types approved under R42. The rear lamp is not a vehicle type approved under R42, so this numbering rule does not apply.

Covers communication of approval or refusal of vehicle types to Contracting Parties using the annex 1 form and vehicle structure drawings. This is an administrative procedure for vehicle-type bumper approval and does not apply to the rear lamp product.

Requires an international approval mark on every vehicle conforming to an R42 approved vehicle type. The product is a rear lamp module and not a vehicle, so the vehicle approval-mark obligation does not apply to it.

Paragraph 5.6 applies to the approval mark on the vehicle. The rear lamp specification does not describe an approval mark or a vehicle data plate, so this obligation does not attach to the lamp.
Paragraph 5.7 places the approval mark close to the vehicle data plate. This is a vehicle marking obligation and does not apply to the rear lamp component.
Paragraph 5.8 only refers to Annex 2 for examples of approval mark arrangements. It imposes no product obligation on the rear lamp.
Paragraph 6 is a section heading with no obligation of its own.

Paragraph 6.1 is the lead-in to the post-impact requirements for the vehicle. The product is a rear lamp for an M1 passenger car, so the lamp is within the vehicle-level scope. The specific lighting obligation is carried by 6.1.1, so no separate requirement is listed here.

Paragraph 6.1.1 requires lighting and signalling devices to keep operating and remain visible after the low-speed impact test. The product includes rear position, stop, and reversing lamps on an M1 vehicle, so this applies to the rear lamp module as installed.

requirements.text: After each Annex 3 impact test, the rear lighting and signalling devices (rear position, stop and reversing lamps) shall continue to operate correctly and remain visible.
requirements.quote: The lighting and signalling devices shall continue to operate correctly and to remain visible.
requirements.reason: The spec lists rear position, stop and reversing lamps as main parts of an M1 vehicle rear lamp, which are lighting and signalling devices within the scope of 6.1.1.

requirements.text: If the factory-fitted lighting devices' adjustment is disturbed by the impact, it may be corrected to the required specifications by the normal means of adjustment; bulbs may be replaced in the event of filament failure.
requirements.quote:
Should the
adjustment of the factory-fitted lighting devices be disturbed, it may be corrected to conform to the required
specifications, provided this can be done by the normal means of adjustment. Bulbs may be replaced in the event
of filament failure.
requirements.reason: The spec describes factory-fitted rear lamp functions. The adjustment and bulb-replacement allowance applies to those devices; the spec does not state whether the lamps use bulbs or LED modules, so this allowance is conditional.

decisions.reason: Paragraph 6.1.2 concerns bonnet, boot lid, and door operability and side-door latching. The rear lamp module does not include these closures.

Paragraph 6.1.4 concerns the vehicle exhaust system. The rear lamp specification does not include any exhaust component.
Paragraph 6.1.5 concerns propulsion, suspension, steering, and braking systems. The rear lamp module is not one of these systems, and the rear lamp is not a driver-assist sensor.
Paragraph 7 is a heading for modifications of the vehicle type. It imposes no product obligation on the rear lamp.

The specification describes a rear lamp module (position, stop, reversing lamps, lens, retro-reflector), which is not a protective device, so this clause does not apply to the product.

Paragraph 8 is a section heading (Conformity of production) with no substantive obligation. R42 scope does not cover the rear lamp described in the specification.

Paragraph 8.1 requires vehicles bearing an R42 approval mark to conform to the approved type, particularly regarding features affecting impact behaviour of structural parts and components. This concerns the vehicle's protective devices under R42. The rear lamp is not a protective device within R42 scope, so the clause does not apply to this product.

Paragraph 8.2 describes random conformity checks on serially manufactured vehicles bearing the R42 approval mark. It is an administrative verification process tied to R42 scope (protective devices), not a requirement on the rear lamp component.

Paragraph 8.3 states that conformity checks are generally limited to measurements and may include paragraph 6 checks on vehicles. These checks relate to R42 protective-device testing for vehicles, which is outside the scope of the rear lamp described in the specification.
Paragraph 9 is a section heading (Penalties for non-conformity of production) with no substantive obligation. R42 scope does not cover the rear lamp.

Paragraph 9.1 allows withdrawal of an R42 vehicle-type approval for failure to meet paragraph 8.1 or paragraph 6 tests. This is an approval administration rule tied to R42 protective-device scope and does not impose an obligation on the rear lamp.

Paragraph 9.2 concerns notification between Contracting Parties of an approval withdrawal ("APPROVAL WITHDRAWN"). It is an inter-administration procedure under R42 and does not apply to the rear lamp product.

UN R42 scope (context clause 1) covers only the behaviour of front and rear protective devices (bumpers) of M1 vehicles in low-speed collisions. Item 15 concerns the position of the R42 approval mark on the vehicle. R42 applies to vehicle front and rear protective devices, and the rear lamp module is not one of them. The spec gives no protective-device or vehicle-level approval mark context.
Item 16 is the place field in the R42 approval communication form. It is administrative and tied to the R42 protective-device approval, which does not cover this rear lamp module.
Item 17 is the date field in the R42 approval communication form. It is administrative and tied to the R42 protective-device approval, which does not cover this rear lamp module.
Item 18 is the signature field in the R42 approval communication form. It is administrative and tied to the R42 protective-device approval, which does not cover this rear lamp module.

Item 19 lists documents annexed to the R42 approval communication, including drawings of protective devices and their position on the vehicle. R42 governs protective devices (bumpers), not the rear lamp module described in the spec, so this documentation obligation does not apply.

Annex 2 shows arrangements of approval marks for R42 (front and rear protective devices, e.g. bumpers) and for combined approvals with other regulations. The rear lamp spec describes no protective device and no vehicle-level R42 approval, so the mark arrangement does not apply to this product.

Annex 3 is the R42 low-speed-impact test procedure, which verifies whether the vehicle's protective devices meet R42. It is a vehicle-level crash test. The product is a rear lamp module, not a vehicle or protective device, so this test procedure does not apply.

Impactor orientation for the R42 low-speed impact test. It is test set-up geometry and does not apply to the rear lamp module.

This is a heading for the R42 longitudinal impact test on the vehicle's front and rear surfaces. It creates no obligation for a rear lamp.

decisions.reason: Paragraph 6.22 governs adaptive front lighting systems (AFS) by reference to headlamp requirements. The product is a rear lamp module with rear position, stop, reversing, and retro-reflector functions only, so no front AFS is in scope.
Paragraph 6.22.1 addresses the presence of AFS on motor vehicles. The product is a rear lamp and has no AFS function.
Paragraph 6.22.2 sets the number and approval of AFS units under UN R149. The product is a rear lamp with no AFS unit.
Paragraph 6.22.3 covers AFS arrangement. The product is a rear lamp module, not an AFS.
Paragraph 6.22.4 sets the neutral position of the AFS before testing. The product has no AFS, so this does not apply.
Paragraph 6.22.4.1 sets width and height requirements for AFS lighting units. The product is a rear lamp with no AFS function.
Paragraph 6.22.4.1.1 covers symmetric placement of AFS lighting units at the front. The product is a rear lamp and does not provide an AFS.
Paragraph 6.22.4.1.2 covers additional AFS lighting units. The product is a rear lamp with no AFS units.
Paragraph 6.22.4.1.3 covers the height of additional AFS lighting units. The product is a rear lamp with no AFS units.
Paragraph 6.22.4.1.4 covers the width placement of passing-beam AFS units. The product is a rear lamp with no passing-beam AFS.
Paragraph 6.22.4.2 requires AFS lighting units to be mounted at the front. The product is a rear lamp, so this does not apply.

Paragraph 6.22.5 covers geometric visibility angles for AFS lighting functions and modes, which are front headlamp functions. The product's rear position, stop, and reversing functions are not AFS functions.

Paragraph 6.22.6 sets the orientation of an adaptive front-lighting system (AFS) to the neutral basic passing-beam facing the front. The product is a rear lamp with rear position, stop, reversing and retro-reflector functions, and the spec lists no AFS or passing-beam unit.
Heading for vertical inclination of the front AFS basic passing-beam. The product has no front passing-beam or cut-off, so the clause does not apply.

Concerns the manufacturer's initial downward inclination of the front passing-beam cut-off, marked on the vehicle near the front lighting system. The rear lamp spec describes no front lighting system or passing-beam cut-off.
Requires the downward inclination of the passing-beam cut-off to stay within limits under static loading. This applies to front dipped/AFS beams, which the rear lamp does not include.
Covers passing-beam cut-offs formed by several beams from different front lighting units. The product has no passing beam; its functions are rear position, stop, reversing and retro-reflection.
Heading for the headlamp levelling device, which is a front headlamp feature. The rear lamp spec contains no headlamp or levelling device.
Requires an automatic levelling device where needed for front passing-beam compliance. The product has no front beam and no levelling device, so the clause does not apply.
Covers the failure mode of a front headlamp levelling device so the passing beam does not move less downward. The product has no such device.
Horizontal orientation of the cut-off kink for front lighting units, projected on the screen. The rear lamp has no cut-off and no front lighting unit.
Measuring procedure for the vertical inclination of the front passing-beam or AFS cut-off across loading conditions. The product has no passing beam or cut-off to measure.
Heading for electrical connections of the AFS main-beam lighting. The product is a rear lamp with no AFS or main-beam (front) lighting, so the clause does not apply.
Heading for main-beam lighting provided by the AFS. The rear lamp spec describes no main-beam or AFS, and the product's functions are rear signalling only.

Paragraph 6.22.7.1.1 governs switching of main-beam lighting units of an AFS headlamp (the AFS main-beam changeover from dipped-beam). The product is a rear lamp with rear position, stop, reversing and retro-reflector functions, and the spec lists no headlamp, main-beam, dipped-beam or AFS function.

Paragraph 6.22.7.1.2 covers adaptive main-beam control driven by sensors detecting ambient light and other vehicles' lamps. This is an AFS headlamp function. The rear lamp spec does not include an adaptive main-beam or any sensor-controlled headlamp system.
Paragraph 6.22.7.1.3 concerns manual ON/OFF and deactivation of main-beam headlamps, adaptive or not. The product has no main-beam headlamp, so the clause does not apply to a rear lamp.
Paragraph 6.22.7.1.4 allows dipped-beams to stay on with main-beams. This is a headlamp beam-combination rule. The rear lamp spec contains no dipped-beam or main-beam function.

Paragraph 6.22.7.1.5 addresses concealable headlamp units and their raised position in relation to additional headlamps used for daylight flashing signals. The product is a rear lamp with no concealable headlamp units.

Paragraph 6.22.7.2 sets passing-beam changeover and gas-discharge source behaviour for headlamps. The product is a rear lamp with LED rear position, stop and reversing functions and no passing-beam headlamp.
Paragraph 6.22.7.3 applies the electrical-connection requirements to dipped-beam headlamp switching. The product has no dipped-beam headlamp, so this clause does not apply.
Paragraph 6.22.7.4 governs automatic operation of AFS lighting functions (passing-beam classes and main-beam adaptation). The product is not an AFS headlamp and the spec describes no AFS.
Paragraph 6.22.7.4.1 sets activation of the class C AFS passing-beam mode. This is an AFS headlamp mode, and the rear lamp spec has no passing-beam or AFS function.
Paragraph 6.22.7.4.2 sets conditions for the class V AFS passing-beam mode (speed and road-lighting conditions). It applies to headlamp AFS modes, not to a rear lamp.
Paragraph 6.22.7.4.3 sets conditions for the class E AFS passing-beam mode (speed and motorway conditions). It is an AFS headlamp mode rule and does not apply to the rear lamp.

Paragraph 6.22.7.4.4 sets conditions for the class W AFS passing-beam mode (wet road or wiper operation) and front fog lamp interaction. It is an AFS headlamp rule and does not apply to the rear lamp.

Paragraph 6.22.7.4.5 governs changes between passing-beam classes (C, V, E, W) and bending modes of an Adaptive Front-lighting System (AFS). The product spec describes a rear lamp with rear position, stop, reversing, and retro-reflector functions, with no passing beam, AFS, or steering-linked bending light. The clause does not apply.

Paragraph 6.22.7.5 requires the driver to be able to set an AFS to neutral and back to automatic. The product is a rear lamp with no AFS and no driver-selectable beam control, so the clause does not apply.
Paragraph 6.22.8 is a heading for AFS tell-tales. The product has no AFS or headlamp tell-tale function, so it does not apply.

Paragraph 6.22.8.1 applies the headlamp tell-tale provisions of 6.1.8 (main beam) and 6.2.8 (dipped beam) to parts of an AFS. The product is a rear lamp with stop, position, and reversing functions and no headlamp or AFS, so the clause does not apply.
Paragraph 6.22.8.2 requires a failure tell-tale for an AFS. The product has no AFS control signals, so the clause does not apply.
Paragraph 6.22.8.3 requires a tell-tale when an adaptive main beam is active. The product has no main beam, adaptive or otherwise, so the clause does not apply.
Paragraph 6.22.8.4 concerns an optional tell-tale for a system state under UN R149. The product has no AFS or UN R149 system, so the clause does not apply.
Paragraph 6.22.9 is a heading for other AFS requirements. It creates no obligation and the product has no AFS.

Paragraph 6.22.9.1 requires headlamp cleaning devices for AFS units contributing to the Class C passing beam, where flux exceeds 2,000 lm. The product is a rear lamp that has no passing beam or AFS, so the clause does not apply.
Paragraph 6.22.9.2 permits Driver Assistance Projection from AFS passing-beam or adaptive main-beam units. The product is a rear lamp with no such units, so the clause does not apply.
Paragraph 6.22.9.3 is a heading for verifying AFS automatic operation. It creates no obligation and the product has no AFS.
Paragraph 6.22.9.3.1 requires the applicant to demonstrate AFS control signals and automatic operation compliance. The product is a rear lamp with no AFS, so the clause does not apply.

Paragraph 6.22.9.3.2 verifies AFS automatic passing-beam operation by test drive. The product is a rear lamp module with rear position, stop, reversing and retro-reflector functions. The specification describes no AFS, headlamp or passing beam, so the clause does not apply.
Paragraph 6.22.9.3.3 covers documentation of the AFS overall performance and safety concept. The product has no AFS or adaptive front lighting, so this does not apply to a rear lamp.
Paragraph 6.22.9.3.4 concerns adaptation of the main beam in AFS headlamps. The product is a rear lamp with no main beam or headlamp function.
Heading for main-beam adaptation, which applies to adaptive headlamps. The rear lamp product has no main beam.
Requires the sensor system controlling main-beam adaptation to comply. The product has no adaptive main beam and no sensor system described in the specification.
Sensor detection field for main-beam adaptation. The rear lamp has no main beam or sensor system for this purpose.
Sensor sensitivity for main-beam adaptation. The product specification has no such sensor or headlamp function.
Requires adaptive main beam to switch off above 7,000 lx ambient illuminance. The product is a rear lamp without an adaptive main beam.
Aggregate maximum reference intensity for main-beam lighting units. The rear lamp (rear position, stop, reversing, retro-reflector) has no main-beam lighting unit.
Owner's manual explanation for temporary use in territory with opposite traffic direction, applying to headlamp main/dipped beam provisions. The rear lamp has no headlamp beam to adjust.

The emergency stop signal is mandatory on motor vehicles and is given by simultaneous operation of all stop or direction-indicator lamps. The product is a rear lamp for an M1 passenger car and includes a stop lamp, so the stop lamp function is within scope.
