Annex 6 para 5.4.1 is the rocking procedure for M1 vehicles before dipped-beam inclination measurement. It is a vehicle test procedure, not an obligation on a rear lamp component, and the spec has no dipped-beam function.
Annex 6 para 5.4.2 is a heading for M2, M3 and N category suspension treatment in the dipped-beam inclination test. The product is an M1 rear lamp, so this does not apply.
Annex 6 para 5.4.2.1 is an alternative-method clause for M2, M3 and N vehicles in the dipped-beam inclination test. The product is an M1 rear lamp with no dipped-beam function, so it does not apply.

Annex 6 para 5.4.2.2 is part of the dipped-beam headlamp inclination-versus-load test procedure (rocking the vehicle by varying load). The rear lamp spec describes only rear position, stop, reversing lamps, outer lens and retro-reflector, with no dipped-beam headlamp or levelling function, so this test does not apply to the product.

Annex 6 para 5.4.2.3 concerns activating suspension and parts affecting dipped-beam inclination on a vibration rig. The product is a rear lamp module with no dipped-beam function, so the clause does not apply.

Annex 6 para 5.4.3 covers vehicles with non-conventional suspension measured for dipped-beam inclination with the engine running. The product is a rear lamp, not a vehicle or a dipped-beam headlamp system, so the clause does not apply.

Annex 6 para 5.5 sets out measurement of dipped-beam inclination variation and manual headlamp-levelling adjustment. The rear lamp spec contains no dipped-beam headlamp or levelling system, so the clause does not apply.
Annex 6 para 5.5.1 sets the measurement limits and safety margin for dipped-beam inclination variation. The product has no dipped-beam function, so this does not apply to the rear lamp.

Annex 6 para 5.5.2 governs repeat measurements when dipped-beam inclination results fall outside the safety margin. The rear lamp has no dipped-beam inclination to measure, so the clause does not apply.
Annex 6 para 5.5.3 is a procedural header for repeated dipped-beam inclination measurements by loading condition. It applies to headlamp levelling tests, which the rear lamp spec does not include.
Annex 6 para 5.5.3.1 defines the averaging of three dipped-beam inclination measurements. The product is a rear lamp with no dipped-beam inclination measurement, so the clause does not apply.
Annex 6 para 5.5.3.2 governs a further series of dipped-beam inclination measurements. The rear lamp spec has no dipped-beam function, so the clause does not apply.
Annex 6 para 5.5.3.3 covers hysteresis loops in automatic headlamp-levelling systems. The product has no headlamp-levelling system, so the clause does not apply.
Annex 6 para 5.5.4 sets pass criteria for dipped-beam inclination variation under loading. The rear lamp spec describes no dipped-beam headlamp, so the clause does not apply.
Annex 6 para 5.5.5 allows the manufacturer to choose a different initial inclination value for dipped-beam headlamp levelling. The rear lamp has no such function, so the clause does not apply.

Annex 7 covers the indication of downward inclination of dipped-beam headlamp cut-off and front fog lamp cut-off. The product is a rear lamp module (rear position, stop, reversing lamps and retro-reflector), with no headlamp or front fog lamp function.
Annex 8 sets controls for headlamp-levelling devices referred to in paragraph 6.2.6.2.2. The specified rear lamp has no headlamp-levelling device or headlamp function.

Annex 12 para 2.3 states that urban test areas must include roads with and without illumination for the adaptive main-beam test drive. This is a headlamp test-course condition and does not apply to the rear lamp.
Annex 12 para 2.4 defines country-road test sections for the adaptive main-beam headlamp test drive. The rear lamp is not a headlamp with main-beam control, so the clause does not apply.
Annex 12 para 2.5 defines multi-lane and country road geometry for the adaptive main-beam headlamp test drive. It is not applicable to the rear lamp product.
Annex 12 para 2.6 requires dense traffic situations in the adaptive main-beam headlamp test drive. The rear lamp has no such headlamp function, so this clause does not apply.

The photometric performance shall be checked:

When equipped with light source(s) at 6.75 V, 13.5 V or 28.0 V, the luminous intensity values produced shall be
corrected. For filament light source(s) the correction factor is the ratio between the reference luminous flux and
the mean value of the luminous flux found at the voltage applied (6.75 V, 13.5 V or 28.0 V).

added together.

requirements. The luminous intensity distribution after one minute of operation can be calculated from the
luminous intensity distribution after 30 minutes of operation by applying at each test point the ratio of luminous

results.reason: R148 scope covers position, stop and reversing lamps, which this rear lamp combines. Paragraph 3.5 requires conformity of production procedures to follow 1958 Agreement Schedule 1 and the paragraph 6 requirements. The candidate keeps both.

Paragraph 3.7 is a conditional duty on the approval holder to inform the granting authority if manufacture of an approved lamp ceases completely. The candidate keeps that condition, and the rear lamp falls within R148 scope. The spec does not say whether production has stopped, but the condition is preserved in the candidate's wording.

Paragraph 4.1 requires each lamp submitted for approval to meet paragraphs 4 and 5. The rear lamp's position, stop and reversing functions fall within R148 scope, and the candidate restates the clause accurately.

R148 scope covers position, stop and reversing lamps, which the product has. Paragraph 4.2 applies sections 5 and 6 of R48, 53, 74 or 86 to each lamp and its vehicle category, where verification at type approval is feasible. The candidate keeps that condition and applies it to M1.

Paragraph 4.3 applies to all lamps within R148 scope. It requires satisfactory operation and retained prescribed characteristics in normal use despite vibration. The candidate states this accurately, and the product is an exterior lamp that falls under it.
R148 scope covers position, stop and reversing lamps, and the product has all three. Paragraph 3.3.3.1 requires lamps to bear the approval marking, and the candidate states that without changing it.
The product's stop lamp is within the R148 scope. Paragraph 3.3.3.2 requires lamps to bear the applicant's trade name or mark, and the candidate matches that.

The clause applies to the lamp's approval marking location, and the product has an outer lens and housing. The candidate keeps the source condition that the marked part is not designed to be separated from the transparent light-emitting part.

Paragraph 3.3.4.2 requires the approval marking to be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood, boot lid or a door is opened. The candidate keeps the "if any / where applicable" limit on the LED substitute light source category. The lamp is fitted to an M1 car, so the rule applies.

Annex 8 states the spot-check acceptance rule accurately (Table 1, per grouping of characteristics). But R128 scope (clause 1) covers only the LED light sources shown in Annex 1, which are intended for use in approved lamps. The spec says only "LED modules on PCB". It does not say these are replaceable, Annex 1 category LED light sources approved under R128. They could be integrated, non-replaceable modules outside R128. The Annex 8 sampling plan is also a conformity-of-production check on LED light source production, not a requirement on a rear lamp. The spec doesn't show that the modules are R128-approved light sources, so the match rests on a shared keyword (LED). Missing evidence: whether the LED modules are R128 Annex 1 light sources.

The product is a rear lamp with position, stop and reversing functions, which are in UN R148 scope. Paragraph 3.3.2.1 makes the circled E and country number part of the approval marking, and 3.3.3.1 requires lamps to bear that marking.
The stop lamp function is in R148 scope. Paragraph 3.3.2.2 requires the sequential number of the approval number to be placed close to the approval mark.

The position, stop and reversing lamps are R148 light-signalling lamps. Paragraph 3.3.2.3 requires the identifying symbols from 3.2.4 as part of the approval marking. The candidate's 'for the functions it provides' wording is a reasonable reading of that.

The reversing lamp is in R148 scope. Paragraph 3.3.2.4 requires the regulation number, the letter R and the two-digit amendment series in force at the time of approval. The candidate matches this closely.

Clause 3.1.2.7(a) requires two complete lamp samples with the application, unless otherwise specified for the relevant lamp. The product is a rear lamp with position, stop and reversing functions, which fall within the R148 scope. The candidate keeps the "unless otherwise specified" condition. It leaves out the symmetrical-lamp allowance, which does not change the obligation.

Clause 3.2.1 requires a separate approval for each lamp listed in paragraph 1. Position, stop and reversing lamps are all listed in the R148 scope, and the spec lists each as a main part. The candidate names only these three lamps, so it does not claim the retro-reflector is covered.

Clause 3.2.2 covers grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps in one unit. The spec describes several light functions combined in a single housing. The candidate states the condition that each lamp must satisfy R148 or another Regulation.

Clause 3.2.3 says approval shall be granted if the submitted lamp type meets the requirements. The product is a lamp type that would be submitted under paragraph 3.1. The candidate keeps the conditional wording. It leaves out the interdependent-system sentence, which is not needed for this obligation. The duty falls on the approval authority, but it still applies to this product's approval.

UN R148 covers position, stop and reversing lamps, and the product has all three. Clause 3.3.4.5 requires the approval marking and the applicable other markings to be affixed on the lamp. The candidate keeps the "where they apply" limit.

The product combines several lamp functions and a retro-reflector in one housing. Clause 3.3.5.1 allows a single approval mark on combined lamps, located anywhere on them, if the conditions in 3.3.5.1.1 and 3.3.5.1.2 are met. The candidate states this as an option, not a mandate. It does not repeat the condition that the lamps comply with several UN Regulations, but this is implied. The spec does not list the approvals actually held.

Clause 3.3.5.1.1 requires a single approval mark on combined lamps to be visible after installation. The product is a combined lamp. The candidate keeps the condition that this applies only if a single mark is used.

Clause 3.3.5.1.2 says no light-transmitting part of the combined lamps can be removed without also removing the single approval mark. The product has a light-transmitting outer lens. The candidate keeps the single-mark condition.

Clause 3.3.5.2 sets the minimum size of a single approval mark's components. It must not be less than the minimum for the smallest individual mark under the pertinent UN Regulations. The product is a combined lamp, and the candidate keeps the single-mark condition.

Clause 3.4.1 requires every modification of an approved lamp type to be notified to the Type Approval Authority that approved it. The product is a lamp type within R148 scope. The spec does not state whether it is approved, so the obligation applies once it is.

The rear lamp has LED modules on a PCB, so it is an electrical/electronic sub-assembly under 2.8. It also has stop and rear position lamp functions, which clause 2.12(c)(i) lists as immunity-related. The 6.10.3 exemption for ESAs with no immunity-related functions therefore does not apply. Clause 6.8.1 requires radiated immunity testing by the Annex 9 methods, and the candidate says this.

The ESA applies for the reasons given for 6.8.1. The candidate's Table 2a and 2b levels match clause 6.8.2.1: 60 V/m stripline, 75 V/m TEM cell, 30 V/m ALSE below 2 GHz and 10 V/m ALSE above 2 GHz. It also keeps the 90 per cent band versus whole-band split.

Clause 6.8.2.2 sets the pass criterion for the Annex 9 tests as no degradation of immunity-related functions. The spec's stop lamp and rear position lamp match the optical functions listed in 2.12(c)(i). The candidate states this criterion correctly.

Clause 6.9.1 requires ISO 7637-2 pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b at the Table 3b levels, with FPSC per ISO 7637-1. The rear lamp is an ESA with immunity-related functions, so this applies. The candidate leaves out the starting profile, which only applies to ESAs for internal combustion vehicles. That is acceptable because the spec does not say whether the vehicle is ICE. It also does not say whether the system is 12 V or 24 V, but Table 3b gives levels for both.
The scope clause lists position lamps, stop lamps and reversing lamps. The spec says the rear lamp has all three functions, so UN R148 applies to it for those functions.

Clause 3.1.2 and 3.1.2.1 require drawings that identify the lamp type and category. They must show the mounting positions, the axis and centre of reference, the limit of the apparent surface of the function(s), and the space for the approval marking. The candidate keeps these core items and leaves out the conditional items (e)–(g). The product is a type-approvable lamp with several functions, so the requirement applies.

Clause 3.1.2.2 requires a brief technical description. It must give the light source category or module code where the source is replaceable. It must also give the make and type of any control gear that is not part of the lamp. The candidate keeps these conditions. The spec does not say whether the LED modules are replaceable, so the conditional items may not apply. Because the candidate wording is conditional, it still matches the clause.

UN R148 clause 4.7.1 covers position, stop and reversing lamps, and the product has all three. The candidate keeps the clause's conditions: the restriction proviso for replaceable sources, and the light source module and non-replaceable alternatives. The spec lists "LED modules on PCB" as the light source. This is the kind of source the clause permits, so the requirement applies. The spec does not say whether the LEDs are replaceable or non-replaceable, but that does not change the obligation.

UN R148 covers position, stop and reversing lamps, and this rear lamp has all three. Paragraph 4.7.2.3 says light signalling devices must not generate radiated or power-line disturbances that malfunction other vehicle electrical or electronic systems. The candidate keeps that wording. The footnote says EMC compliance is relevant to the vehicle type, which does not change the obligation.

Paragraph 4.8.1 sets general conditions for all photometric and colorimetric measurements, and the sub-paragraphs that follow give those conditions. The rear lamp's light functions and red lens fall under this regulation. The candidate accurately restates the clause.

Paragraph 4.8.1.4 requires stray reflections to be avoided by appropriate masking during photometric measurements. It applies to this lamp's photometric testing. The candidate repeats the clause word for word.

UN R148 covers stop lamps, and the product has a stop lamp. Clause 5.5.1 requires the emitted light to meet Table 7 for luminous intensity and standard light distribution. The candidate leaves out the "each of two samples" wording, which concerns approval testing and doesn't change the obligation. The spec doesn't state the stop lamp category (S1–S4, MS), so the exact Table 7 values can't be fixed from it.

Clause 5.5.2 sets the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility by pointing to Table 7. Table 7 has a matching column, and the product has a stop lamp. The candidate keeps that reference to Table 7.

UN R148 covers position lamps and stop lamps, and the product has a rear position function. Clause 4.8.3.1(a) and (b) set the reference-axis minimum and the visible-direction maximum, and the candidate states both accurately.
The product has a stop lamp function, which is in R148 scope. Clause 4.8.3.1(c) and (d) set the off-axis and geometric-visibility minimums, and the candidate keeps the two alternatives from (c).
Clause 4.8.3.6 requires luminous intensity compliance tests to follow Annex 8. The product's stop and position lamp functions are subject to luminous intensity requirements, so this applies.

Clause 4.9 requires colour to be measured inside the Annex 3 light distribution grid for the function, with no sharp colour variation outside it. The product's red-tinted lens makes the emitted colour relevant. The candidate omits the reference to the 4.8 test procedure and the non-replaceable light source note, which does not change the obligation.

UN R148 paragraph 5.8.7 sits under 5.8 Reversing lamps (AR) and says the colour of light emitted shall be white. The R148 scope includes reversing lamps, and the product spec lists a reversing lamp. The candidate keeps the clause's meaning and adds no extra condition.

The product has a rear position lamp, so clause 5.2.1 applies. The Table 4 requirement for each of the two samples is stated correctly. The candidate leaves out the 60 cd allowance for a position lamp combined with a stop lamp below the 5° plane. That is a permission, not an extra obligation, so I did not treat the omission as a mismatch. The spec does not give the lamp category (R1, R2, etc.).

Clause 5.2.2 sets the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility by reference to Table 4. It applies to the product's rear position lamp, and the candidate matches the clause.
Clause 5.2.7 requires rear position lamps to emit red light. The product has a rear position lamp with a red-tinted lens, so the clause applies and the candidate states it correctly.

UN R148 scope covers stop lamps, and the product has a stop lamp. Clause 5.5.6 sits under 5.5 (Stop lamps) and says "See paragraph 4.6." for failure provisions. The candidate restates that cross-reference and adds no separate obligation. I did not read the content of 4.6.

Clause 5.5.7 sits under 5.5 (Stop lamps) and requires the emitted light to be red. The product has a stop lamp behind a red-tinted lens, so the clause applies. The candidate keeps the requirement as written. Actual compliance still depends on the final lens and light source.

UN R148 scope (clause 1) covers reversing lamps. The product spec lists a reversing lamp as a main part and reversing illumination as a function. Annex 1 item 9.1.3 is the communication entry for a reversing lamp. It asks whether the lamp may be installed only as part of a pair, with yes/no to be struck out. The candidate keeps that meaning. The spec gives no yes/no value, but the candidate does not invent one.

The clause 4.8.1.7 applies to intensity measurements of the lamp's position, stop and reversing functions. These functions are within the R148 scope. The candidate keeps the "unless otherwise specified" condition.
Clause 4.8.1.8 applies to measurements on this lamp if the results are challenged. The candidate keeps the condition and refers to the sub-clauses 4.8.1.8.1 to 4.8.1.8.3.
Clause 4.8.1.8.1 sets the inverse-square-law measurement distance for challenged results. It applies to the rear position lamp's photometry, and the candidate keeps the challenge condition.
Clause 4.8.1.8.2 requires a receiver angular aperture between 10' and 1 degree for challenged measurements. It applies to the reversing lamp's photometry, and the candidate wording matches it.
Clause 4.8.1.8.3 gives a one-quarter-degree tolerance on the direction of observation for challenged results. It applies to the lamp's photometric directions, and the candidate wording matches it.

Clause 4.8.1.9 requires the apparent surface limits to be determined for a light-signalling lamp. The rear position lamp is one. The candidate keeps the exceptions for rear-registration plate lamps and category 5 and 6 direction indicators. Neither exception applies to this product.

Clause 4.8.2 sets the test voltage unless otherwise specified: 6.75 V, 13.5 V or 28 V depending on the system voltage. It applies to this lamp. The candidate keeps all three options, so the unstated system voltage does not matter.

UN R148 scope covers position, stop and reversing lamps, which are the functions of this rear lamp. Annex 1 item 9.2 is the communication form's concise description by light signalling function and category. It asks for the colour of light emitted and the number, category and kind of light source(s). The candidate keeps these elements. The spec confirms LED light sources but gives no colour or category per function, so those values are left for the applicant to fill in. The retro-reflector is outside R148 but does not affect the lamp functions covered here.

R148 covers position, stop and reversing lamps, which this rear lamp contains. Clause 3.2.3.2 assigns an approval number to each approved lamp type and allows one number for a system of lamps. It bars that number from another lamp type of the same function. The candidate keeps all of this.

Clause 3.2.4 is truncated. It says only that symbols identify the function for which approval was granted. It does not say the symbols must be shown on the lamp, and the marking duty comes from other clauses (3.3.x). The cited text may be incomplete, so the candidate's obligation cannot be confirmed from it.

Table 1 gives the symbols: rear position R1 (steady) and R2 (variable), stop S1 (steady) and S2 (variable), and reversing AR. The product has all three functions. The candidate keeps the steady-or-variable alternatives and does not assume which applies. The 'shall be used' duty is only implied by the Table 1 context.

Clause 3.3.1.1 requires every device of an approved type to have a space large enough for the approval marking and other markings. The rear lamp is such a device. The candidate states this requirement accurately and does not claim the spec shows compliance.
Clause 3.3.1.1.1 requires all markings to be clearly legible and indelible. This applies to the approved rear lamp device's markings.

Clause 3.3.1.2 sets a minimum value of 5 mm for 'a' in the approval marking. This applies to the approved rear lamp. The candidate states the limit correctly and does not claim the spec shows compliance.

results.reason: The product has a reversing lamp, which is in scope of R148 5.8 (Reversing lamps AR). Clause 5.8.1 requires the light from each sample to meet Table 10. The candidate leaves out the optional pair-installation relaxation (30° inwards, at least 25 cd). That relaxation is an alternative route, so the main obligation is preserved.

Table 10 gives category AR as the only reversing lamp entry. Its values are minimum 80 cd, maximum 300 cd in or above the h-plane, maximum 600 cd below the h-plane down to 5°D, maximum 8000 cd below 5°D, and standard light distribution Figure A3-V. The candidate matches these values. The category is inferred from the table's only entry, so the product drawings should confirm it. I did not read paragraph 4.8.3.1 (a), so the "on the axis of reference" wording is assumed from Table 9's equivalent column.

The spec lists a reversing lamp for an M1 car, and UN R148 scope covers reversing lamps. Annex 3 para 2.5 sets the standard light distribution for reversing lamps as measuring points and minimum intensities. The candidate states this without adding numbers or conditions. The clause is more descriptive than imperative, so the match rests on its being the Annex 3 distribution for this lamp.

The spec includes a reversing lamp, which is in R148 scope. Figure A3-V text says its values give the minimum intensities in cd for the various measurement directions, with H=0° and V=0° as the axis of reference. The candidate matches this and states no numeric values that would need the figure itself.

UN R148 scope covers position, stop and reversing lamps, which the M1 rear lamp includes. Clause 6.1.3 sets the 20% unfavourable-deviation limit and refers to Table 12 for minimum values in Annexes 2 and 3. The candidate keeps this meaning. It leaves out that this is a conformity-of-production check, which is minor.

Table 12 is the table that 6.1.3 refers to. It gives the 20% equivalent values for minimum required values, and the stop lamp is covered by R148. The table has no obligation of its own, so the requirement comes from the 6.1.3 lead-in. The candidate states that requirement faithfully for the 20% column.

Clause 6.2 lets the approving authority verify conformity control methods at each production facility at any time, with a normal frequency of once every two years. This applies to production of the R148 rear lamp functions. The candidate omits 'at any time' but keeps the normal two-year frequency.

R148 scope covers position, stop and reversing lamps, which the rear lamp includes. Annex 4 para 1.1 says mechanical and geometric conformity holds if differences stay within inevitable manufacturing deviations. The candidate keeps that condition.

The product has position, stop and reversing lamp functions, which are in R148 scope. Annex 4 para 1.2 says photometric conformity of mass-produced lamps is not contested when a randomly chosen lamp is tested per para 4.8. The candidate matches this.
Annex 4 para 1.3 requires the chromaticity coordinates to be met when tested under para 4.9. The product is a red-lens signalling lamp in R148 scope, so this applies.

Annex 4 para 2 requires the type-approval holder to carry out at least the listed tests at appropriate intervals, in accordance with the Regulation. The candidate is a fair paraphrase. It applies to this rear lamp as an R148 lamp type.
Annex 4 para 2.1 says the conformity tests cover photometric and colorimetric characteristics. The product has photometric signalling functions and a red lens, so this applies.

Annex 3 §1.1 sets the general rule that the figure values are minimum intensities as a percentage of the required minimums, rounded down to three significant digits unless otherwise specified. The product's rear position lamp is a lamp this rule covers. The candidate keeps the "unless specified otherwise" condition. It leaves out the 750 mm mounting-height exception, but it doesn't contradict it.

Annex 3 §1.2 sets the grid-based uniformity rule for light distribution fields shown as a grid. The product has a reversing lamp, and reversing lamps are within the scope of R148. The candidate wording matches the clause.

The second paragraph of Annex 3 §1.2 applies specifically to reversing lamps, and the product has one. The candidate keeps the conditions: visual examination shows substantial local variations, and no intensity between two measured directions may fall below 50% of the lower of the two prescribed minimums.

Annex 3 §2.1 gives the standard light distribution for front and rear position lamps, expressed as minimum intensities as a percentage of those required (Tables 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8). The product's rear position lamp falls within it.

Figure A3-I is titled as the standard light distribution for front and rear position lamps, among others, and the product has a rear position lamp. The clause text available is only the caption, and the grid values are not given. The obligation to meet the figure's distribution is therefore only weakly supported, but it is consistent with §2.1.

UN R150 scope covers retro-reflectors, and the product is an M1 rear lamp with a PMMA prism retro-reflector in the housing. Annex 6 Part 4 para 1 requires retro-reflective devices to keep their prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences they are normally exposed to. The candidate states this obligation accurately. It leaves out the tarnishing and rear-face checks and the ISO 9227 test reference, but these are test details and do not change the design obligation. The spec does not give the retro-reflector's class, but the obligation applies to all retro-reflectors in scope.

The rear lamp includes a PMMA prism retro-reflector, which is a retro-reflector under UN R150 (scope and 4.1). Clause 4.1.4 requires its outer surface to be easy to clean, not rough, and free of protuberances that prevent cleaning. The candidate keeps that meaning.

The same retro-reflector component brings the product under clause 4.1.5. The clause says there shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflector in normal use, and the candidate states this faithfully. The spec does not confirm the housing construction, but that only affects compliance. It does not affect whether the clause applies.
The product includes R148 position, stop and reversing lamps. Annex 4 2.2.1 says conformity tests are generally carried out by the R148 methods, and the candidate matches this.

Annex 4 2.2.2 allows equivalent methods only with the competent authority's consent, and the manufacturer must prove equivalence. The candidate keeps both conditions, and the reversing lamp is in R148 scope.
Annex 4 2.2.3 requires regular calibration of test apparatus and correlation with the competent authority's measurements. The candidate matches this, and the product's lamps are in R148 scope.
Annex 4 2.2.4 makes the R148 methods the reference methods in all cases, especially for administrative verification and sampling. The candidate matches this.
Annex 4 2.3 requires samples to be selected at random from a uniform production batch. The product is a series-produced R148 lamp, so this applies.

Annex 4 2.4 requires photometric measurement of the sampled lamp at the Annex 3 points and the required chromaticity coordinates. The heading says 'measured and recorded', so 'recorded' is acceptable. The red lens makes colorimetry relevant.

Annex 4 2.5 requires a manufacturer statistical study. It also requires acceptability criteria agreed with the authority, giving a minimum 0.95 probability of passing an Annex 5 spot check at 95% confidence. The candidate preserves this. The reason's focus on the outer lens is only loose context.
Annex 5 1.1 treats mechanical and geometric conformity as satisfied if differences stay within inevitable manufacturing deviations. The candidate matches this and applies to the lamp.

Annex 5 1.2(a) says photometric conformity of mass-produced lamps is not contested if no measured value deviates from the paragraph 6.1.3 values for any random lamp. Clause (b) applies only to replaceable light sources, and the spec does not say the LED modules are replaceable, so omitting it is acceptable.

Annex 8 para 2.1 makes the additional time-based check depend on light source technology, and the candidate drops that condition. The product uses LED modules. Para 2.1.2 says an LED-only function is deemed to comply at all points in time if the para 1.2 values are compliant. So the product has no separate additional check at the Table A8-1 times. The spec does not say whether any function mixes LED with another technology, which would trigger para 2.1.3.

The Table A8-1 values are correct: stop 0.2 s, reversing 0.2 s, front and rear position 4 s, all at HV. However, the table applies only through para 2.1, which depends on light source technology. The product is LED-based, and para 2.1.2 deems LED-only functions compliant at all times if the para 1.2 measurements pass. The candidate therefore states an additional check obligation that does not apply to this product as described.

Paragraph 3.1.1.1(c) requires a brief description of the technical specifications of the materials of the retro-reflecting optical unit. The rear lamp contains a retro-reflector, which the spec lists as PMMA with molded prism optics, so the clause applies.

Paragraph 3.1.1.1(d) requires retro-reflector samples in the manufacturer-specified colour, plus the means of fixation if necessary. The spec does not give the colour, but the clause leaves the colour to the manufacturer, so the obligation applies to this retro-reflector.

Paragraph 3.2.1 requires a separate approval for each retro-reflective device within the scope of paragraph 1. The retro-reflector is a retro-reflector device under that scope, so it needs its own approval.

Paragraph 3.2.3 requires an approval number to be assigned to each approved type and marked on the device as set out in paragraph 3.3. This applies to the retro-reflector as an approved device. Paragraph 3.3 itself was not read.

The product has a retro-reflector in a combined rear lamp. That fits R150 Class IB (combined with other signal lamps), which is in scope. Clause 3.2.5 requires identifying symbols, and Table 1 lists them. The spec does not say which symbol applies.
Clause 3.3.1.1 requires every device of an approved type to have enough space for the Unique Identifier or approval marking, plus the other markings. The product's retro-reflector is an R150 device.
Clause 3.3.1.2 requires all markings to be clearly legible and indelible. This applies to the approved retro-reflector device.
Clause 3.3.2.1 defines the approval mark as a circle around the letter E, followed by the number of the approving country. It applies to the approved retro-reflector.
Clause 3.3.2.2 requires the four- to six-digit sequential number of the approval number to be placed close to the approval mark. It applies to the approved retro-reflector.
Annex 5 para 1.3 says lamps with apparent defects are disregarded. R148 scope covers stop, position and reversing lamps, which the product contains.
Annex 5 para 1.4 requires the chromaticity coordinates to be met when tested under para 4.9. The product is a red-lens signalling lamp that falls under R148.
Annex 5 para 2 selects four lamps at random, with the first two marked A and the second two marked B. The product's position lamp is within R148 scope.

Annex 5 para 2.1 says conformity is not contested if all four lamps deviate by no more than 20 per cent. It also allows measurement to stop if both lamps of sample A deviate by no more than 0 per cent. The candidate keeps both conditions.

Annex 5 para 2.2 contests conformity if any specimen of A or B deviates by more than 20 per cent. It requires alignment and repeat sampling within two months, and the Technical Service keeps samples A and B. The candidate matches this.
Annex 5 para 3 selects four lamps at random from stock made after alignment, marked C and D. The candidate matches this.
Annex 5 para 3.1 matches the candidate: the 20 per cent limit for samples C and D, and early termination if both lamps of sample C deviate by no more than 0 per cent.
Annex 5 para 3.2 says conformity is contested if at least one specimen of C or D falls in the bands set out in paras 3.2.1 or 3.2.2. The candidate keeps that structure, though it is brief.
Annex 5 para 3.2.1 covers deviations above 20 per cent but no more than 30 per cent. It requires realignment and a second repeat sampling within two months, which the candidate reflects.
Annex 5 para 3.2.2 withdraws approval and applies para 5 if one specimen of C or D deviates by more than 30 per cent. The candidate matches this.
Annex 5 para 4 selects four lamps at random from stock made after alignment, marked E and F. The candidate matches this.
Annex 5 para 4.1 matches the candidate: the 20 per cent limit for samples E and F, and early termination if both lamps of sample E deviate by no more than 0 per cent.

R23 applies to reversing lamps on M-category vehicles, and the product is an M1 rear lamp with a reversing lamp. Clause 2.1 says the application is submitted by the trade name or mark holder or an accredited representative. The candidate leaves out the optional installation-inclination sentence, but it does not contradict that sentence.

Clause 2.2 requires the application for each reversing lamp type to be accompanied by the items listed in 2.2.1 to 2.2.3. The candidate summarizes those items correctly as drawings, a brief technical description and two samples. The product has a reversing lamp, so the clause applies.

Clause 2.2.1 requires drawings in triplicate that identify the reversing lamp type and show its mounting geometry, reference axis and reference centre. The product has a reversing lamp, so the clause applies. The candidate omits the approval-mark position, but that does not contradict the clause.

Clause 2.2.2 requires a technical description stating the LED light source category or the module identification code. It exempts lamps with non-replaceable light sources, and the candidate keeps that exception. The product uses LED modules, so the clause applies. The candidate leaves out the filament lamp option, which is acceptable because the product has no filament lamp.

Clause 2.2.3 requires two samples to accompany the application. The product has a reversing lamp, so the clause applies. The candidate omits the allowance for identical samples of symmetrical devices, which is a relaxation and not a conflict.

UN R148 covers stop lamps, reversing lamps and position lamps, and the product has all three. Annex 5 para 4.2 sets the conformity-of-production sampling rule: a deviation above 20% in any specimen of samples E or F contests conformity, and the approval is withdrawn under para 5. The candidate keeps that threshold and consequence. The spec does not mention approval status, but this is a production-conformity rule for approved lamps, so applicability is reasonable.

Annex 5 para 5 says approval is withdrawn under para 3.6 as required by paras 4.1 and 4.2. The candidate restates this and keeps the condition that withdrawal follows only when the conformity check requires it. The product's stop and reversing lamp functions are within R148 scope.

results.reason: Clause 4.5 covers assemblies of grouped, combined or incorporated lamps. The product combines several light functions, including a reversing lamp, in one housing. The candidate keeps the condition that each lamp must satisfy this or another Regulation.

Clause 4.5.1 permits, as an option, a single approval mark placed anywhere on the combined lamps if 4.5.1.1 and 4.5.1.2 are met. The product is a combined assembly, and the candidate keeps the optional wording and the conditions.
Clause 4.5.1.1 requires the mark to be visible after installation. This applies when the single combined mark is used on the combined rear lamp, and the candidate keeps that condition.

Clause 4.5.1.2 says no light-transmitting part can be removed without removing the approval mark. The outer lens is a light-transmitting part of the combined assembly, so the clause applies and the candidate matches it.

Clause 4.5.2 requires the identification symbol for each lamp, with the applicable amendment series, to be marked. The product combines several functions, so this applies. The candidate leaves out the placement options in 4.5.2.1 and 4.5.2.2, which is a minor omission.

The product has a reversing lamp, and UN R23 covers reversing lamps. Paragraph 10.1 lets the approval be withdrawn if the requirements are not met or the lamp does not conform to the approved type. The candidate frames this as a compliance duty and says only that withdrawal "may" happen, so it keeps the source's conditional wording. The spec does not say whether the lamp is approved, so the match relies on the product falling within R23's approval scope.

Paragraph 11 requires an approval holder who completely stops making an approved reversing lamp type to tell the approving authority. The candidate keeps that condition ("if the approval holder"). The product's reversing lamp falls within R23. The spec does not name an approval holder, so the duty applies only if the lamp type is approved.

The product has a reversing lamp, which UN R23 covers. Annex 3 clause 1.1 requires stray reflections to be avoided by appropriate masking during photometric measurements. The candidate keeps that meaning.

Annex 3 clause 1.2.1 sets the inverse-square-law distance requirement, and it applies only when measurement results are challenged. The candidate keeps that condition. The product has a reversing lamp.

Annex 3 clause 1.2.2 requires the receiver to subtend an angle of 10' to 1° from the reference centre, and it applies only when results are challenged. The candidate matches this and keeps the condition.

Annex 3 clause 1.2.3 treats the intensity requirement for a direction as met if the required intensity is obtained within a quarter of a degree of that direction. It applies only when results are challenged. The candidate matches this and keeps the condition.

Annex 3 clause 2.1 sets out the reference axis for reversing lamps. On the vehicle it is horizontal, parallel to the median longitudinal plane, oriented in the required direction of visibility, and passes through the centre of reference. The candidate reflects this, and the product has a reversing lamp.

Annex 6 Part 4 clause 2 applies the saline mist test to the retro-reflective device, or to the lamp if the device is combined with a light. The product is a rear lamp with an integral retro-reflector, so the post-test requirement of clause 4.1 applies. The candidate keeps the clause's wording that the sample shall show no excessive corrosion liable to impair efficiency. The cited evidence (the metallised lamp reflector surface) is not the retro-reflector itself, but the obligation does not depend on it.

Clause 4.2 sets limits on the coefficient of retro-reflection RA in cd/m²/lx. In R150, RA is the measure for retro-reflective marking materials and plates. Tables 6 and 7 are the RA tables for marking materials. The product's retro-reflector is a device of the Class I type, which R150 measures by RI (Table 3). The spec does not say the product has marking material or plates with RA areas. The candidate's own reason concedes the Table 9/10 values were not confirmed. I did not find Tables 9 and 10 in my searches. Applying clause 4.2 to the product's retro-reflector is therefore not supported.

R3 applies to retro-reflecting devices on M-category vehicles, and the product has a retro-reflector. Paragraph 4.4 requires the markings to be legible and indelible, and the candidate says the same.

The product's retro-reflector falls within R3 scope. The candidate keeps the condition 'conforming to a type approved under this Regulation'. The class is not stated in the spec, but the clause does not need it for applicability.

The spec describes several lamp functions and a retro-reflector in one housing, which is a grouped or combined unit. Paragraph 5.6 requires each lamp in such a unit to satisfy R3 or another Regulation, and the candidate matches that.

Paragraph 5.6.1 allows a single approval mark for a combined unit, provided it is visible after installation (5.6.1.1). The candidate keeps the condition that this applies only if the single-mark option is used. The product is a combined unit.

Paragraph 5.6.1.2 applies when a single approval mark is used on a combined unit. In that case no light-transmitting part may be removed without removing the mark. The outer lens transmits light, and the candidate keeps the single-mark condition.

Paragraph 5.6.2 requires the identification symbol of each lamp in a grouped or combined unit to be marked, with the series of amendments for each Regulation under which approval was granted. The product combines several lamp functions, so the clause applies. The candidate omits the placement options in 5.6.2.1 and 5.6.2.2, which does not change the obligation.

R48 paragraph 1 covers M and N vehicles, and the M1 rear lamp is a light-signalling device. Paragraph 5.1 requires such devices to be fitted so that they keep their prescribed characteristics under normal use and vibration. The candidate keeps that condition and the aim of vehicle compliance.

The second sentence of 5.1 says it must not be possible for the lamps to be inadvertently maladjusted. It applies to the fitted rear lamp, which includes the rear position lamp, and the candidate wording matches it.

Clause 3.2.7 of UN R48 applies to vehicles of categories M and N, and the product is for an M1 car. It requires a description of the electric power supply conditions for the devices listed in 2.5.1, 2.5.2, 2.5.4, 2.5.6 and 2.5.7. The spec describes an M1 rear lamp with rear position, stop and reversing functions, so these are covered. This sentence of 6.1.1 is a conditional allowance, not an obligation on the product. R48 scope covers M and N vehicles, and the product is an M1 rear lamp. Para 5.8 sets the measurement method: highest point for maximum height and lowest point for minimum height, of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis. The 5.15 colour table gives red for the rear position lamp, and the product has one.
The 5.15 colour table gives red for the stop lamp, and the product has one.
The 5.15 colour table gives white for the reversing lamp, and the product has one.
The 5.15 colour table gives red for the rear retro-reflector, both non-triangular and triangular. The product has a retro-reflector and the spec places it in a rear lamp.

Paragraph 5.16.1 requires the number of lamps mounted on the vehicle to equal the number in the individual specifications. This applies to the product's rear lamp functions. The candidate keeps that reference to the individual specifications and does not invent a count.

Paragraph 3.1 sets out who submits a vehicle-type approval application. That is an administrative duty of the vehicle manufacturer or its representative. The product is a rear lamp module, and the spec says nothing about a vehicle-type application or its applicant. The M1 category does not turn this into a product-level requirement.

Paragraph 3.2 is only a lead-in to the document list for a vehicle-type application, and the specific items sit in sub-paragraphs. It places no obligation on a rear lamp component. Applying it to this product would need vehicle-level application facts that the spec does not give.

Paragraph 3.2.2 requires a list of the devices the manufacturer prescribes for the lighting and light-signalling assembly. Each type must be identified, for example by component, approval mark and manufacturer. The rear lamp's position, stop and reversing functions are devices that would belong on that list. The obligation falls on the vehicle application that includes this lamp.

Paragraph 3.2.3 requires a layout drawing of the lighting and light-signalling equipment as a whole, showing where the devices sit on the vehicle. The rear lamp is one of those devices on an M1 vehicle, so it must appear in the drawing.

Paragraph 3.2.5 requires the apparent-surface method to be declared for each lamp, as defined in paragraph 2.5, and recorded in item 10.2 of Annex 1. The product's position, stop and reversing lamps are lamps of that kind. The spec does not state the method, but the clause only requires the declaration, so that gap does not defeat the match.

It says a lamp, even with an approval mark, is deemed not present if it cannot be made to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse. It excepts retro-reflectors. Para 5.11 requires the electrical connections to let the front and rear position lamps, end-outline and side-marker lamps (if present) and the registration plate lamp be switched ON and OFF only simultaneously. The product has a rear position lamp, so this applies. The candidate leaves out the para 5.11.1 exceptions (for example parking lamps), which sit in a separate sub-clause. It does not contradict them.

Clause 5.3 applies to the rear lamp, and the ±3° tolerance and the parallel-axis rules are stated correctly. The candidate turns the manufacturer's fitting instructions into an exception ("unless ... say otherwise"). The clause requires the sampled retro-reflector to be photometrically measured at the points and chromaticity coordinates the Regulation provides. It applies to the spec's retro-reflector and the candidate matches it.

The source says retro-reflectors with apparent defects are disregarded, within the conformity sampling rules. The candidate matches that and it applies to the spec's retro-reflector.
In first repeated sampling, conformity is not contested if every specimen of samples C and D deviates by no more than 20%. The candidate matches this and it applies to the retro-reflector.
If one specimen exceeds 20% but all are within 30%, the manufacturer must align production and a second repeated sampling follows within two months of notification. The candidate matches this.
If one specimen of samples C and D exceeds 30%, approval is withdrawn and paragraph 5 applies. The candidate matches this and it applies to the retro-reflector.

The clause sets a water-penetration test for retro-reflectors using Annex 8 paragraph 1, or Annex 14 paragraph 3 for class IVA. Sample B must pass if sample A fails. The candidate captures this, though it simplifies the Annex 8 versus Annex 14 split and the spec does not state the reflector class.

The signal is a vehicle-level function, and the stop lamp in this lamp is one of the lamps that would be operated. I did not read 6.23.7, so the detail of how the lamps are operated is unchecked.

Annex 9 §1.1 requires COP checks of lamp position in width, height and length. The measured distances must meet each lamp's individual specification. The candidate leaves out the cross-referenced general paragraphs (2.10.2 etc.), which is a minor omission and does not change the meaning.

Listing the rear position and stop lamp functions as the purposes is a reasonable application to this product.

The product is an M1 passenger-car rear lamp, so R53 paragraph 6.8.5 ("Rearwards" for the non-triangular rear retro-reflector) does not apply to it. The spec's statement that the referenced regulations apply to M and N categories does not extend R53 to M1. The shared keyword "retro-reflector" is not enough to establish applicability.

The candidate keeps the clause's meaning and adds no conditions. I did not read the R7 scope paragraph or paragraphs 4.2.1 and 4.2.2. The 4.2.4 text and the R7 definitions were enough to decide.

Paragraph 5.2 of UN R7 requires the devices to keep operating satisfactorily and keep their prescribed characteristics under normal use and vibration. The product includes a rear position lamp and a stop lamp, which are devices UN R7 covers. The candidate's singular wording keeps the clause's conditions, with "devices" read as the lamp. I did not look up R7's scope clause, so applicability rests on the clause's own definitions (1.2, 1.3) and my general knowledge of R7.

The product has a rear position lamp. Clause 4.2.2.2 requires the letter R on a device meeting R7 as a rear position lamp. The letter can be followed by 1 for steady intensity or 2 for variable intensity, or by neither. The candidate keeps the condition that the lamp meets R7.
The product has a stop lamp. Clause 4.2.2.5 requires the letter S followed by figure 1, 2, 3 or 4 on a stop lamp meeting R7. The candidate lists the same four figures and their conditions.

The product combines a rear position lamp and a stop lamp in one housing. Clause 4.2.2.6 requires R, R1 or R2 and S1 or S2, separated by a horizontal dash, on such a combined device. The candidate keeps the condition that both lamps meet R7. The spec does not say whether the two functions are grouped as one device, so this is a small assumption.

Paragraph 4.1.2 applies because the product combines rear position, stop and reversing lamps in one housing. Each lamp must meet UN R7 or another Regulation. The candidate keeps that condition. It omits the headlamp double-filament exception, which does not apply to this product.
The second sentence of 4.1.2 says lamps that fail every applicable Regulation cannot be part of the combined unit. The product is a combined unit that includes a rear position lamp.

Paragraph 4.1.3 requires an approval number for each approved type, and its first two digits show the amendment series. The rear position and stop lamp functions fall under R7 type approval. The duty falls mainly on the approval authority. The spec does not state the approval status.

Paragraph 4.1.5 requires every device conforming to an approved type to bear an approval mark in the space referred to in 3.3, in addition to the 3.1, 3.2 or 3.4 markings. The rear lamp's R7 functions fall under this. The spec does not say where the marking is placed.

Paragraph 4.2.1.1 requires the international approval mark to include a circle around the letter E followed by the approving country's number. This applies to the R7-approved rear position and stop lamp functions.
Paragraph 4.2.1.2 requires the international approval mark to include the approval number from 4.1.3. This applies to the R7-approved lamp functions. The spec does not give the number.

UN R7 covers rear position and stop lamps, and the product is a rear lamp with both. Clause 2.1.5 is conditional on the applicant's choice, and the candidate keeps that condition. Indicating the installation conditions in the communication form matches the clause.

Clause 2.2 is the lead-in saying each device type's application must be accompanied by the listed items. The candidate's reference to 2.2.1–2.2.7 'as applicable' is a fair summary of that list, and the product is a device needing approval.

Clause 2.2.1 requires drawings in triplicate showing mounting positions, the axis of observation and centre of reference, installation conditions under paragraph 6, interdependent lamp combinations, and the approval mark position. The candidate reproduces these. It applies to the rear lamp, which has position and stop functions.

Clause 2.2.2 applies 'with the exception of lamps with non-replaceable light sources', and the candidate drops that exception. The spec only says 'LED modules on PCB' and does not say whether they are replaceable. The unconditional obligation therefore does not preserve the source's limit.

Clause 2.2.4 requires two samples with the application. The candidate states this, and the omitted symmetrical-device allowance and variable-intensity provision are not limits on the obligation. It applies to the rear lamp device.

The spec lists a rear position lamp on an M1 vehicle. Paragraph 6.1 requires reference-axis intensity between the minimum and maximum for each listed function, and rows 6.1.1 to 6.1.3 cover the rear position lamp. The stop-lamp rows are in the separate clause 6.1.4, but the 6.1 intro covers all table rows, so the generalisation is acceptable. The candidate omits the single-lamp and "D" distinction, and the category is not stated in the spec.

The spec lists a stop lamp for braking indication. Clause 6.1.4 gives the S1 to S4 minimum and maximum intensities, read with the 6.1 requirement that they apply in the reference axis. The candidate's wording "declared category" correctly leaves the category open, since the spec does not state it.
The product has a rear position lamp. Clause 6.2.1 sets the off-axis minimum as the 6.1 table minimum multiplied by the Annex 4 percentage for each direction. The candidate states this accurately.

The product's rear position lamp is a light-signalling device. Clause 6.2.2 caps intensity at the 6.1 table maximum in any direction from which the device is visible. The separate 6.2.3 allowance for reciprocally incorporated stop lamps is a distinct clause, and the spec does not say the lamps are reciprocally incorporated.
Clause 6.2.4.1 sets a 0.05 cd minimum throughout the Annex 1 fields for rear position lamps. The product has one, so the candidate matches the clause.
Clause 6.2.4.3 requires observing Annex 4 paragraph 2.2 on local variations of intensity. This applies to the product's rear position lamp, and the candidate keeps that wording.

Clause 6.3 requires intensities to be measured with the light sources continuously alight, and in coloured light for devices emitting red light. The product's lamps are measured under R7, and the red lens appears in the materials table, which is marked representative. The candidate keeps the red-only condition.

Paragraph 11 requires an approval holder who completely ceases to manufacture an R7-approved device to inform the authority that granted the approval. The product has rear position and stop lamp functions, which R7 covers. The candidate keeps the condition that the device is approved under R7. The spec does not say whether the lamp is approved, but the candidate is conditional on that.

Annex 1 sets minimum vertical angles of 15° above and 15° below the horizontal for rear position lamps and stop lamps, with listed exceptions. The product has both lamp functions. The candidate keeps the exception clause. The spec gives no mounting height, so it does not show which exception applies, if any.

UN R7 covers rear position lamps and stop-lamps. The product has both functions, so 3.1 (applicant trade name or mark, legible and indelible) applies. The wording matches the clause. I did not check the reversing lamp, which R7 does not cover, but it does not change this result.

Clause 3.3 requires a space for the approval marking and the 4.2 symbols, shown in the 2.2.1 drawings. It applies to devices submitted for approval, and the rear position and stop functions fall within R7. The candidate keeps the clause's conditions.

Clause 3.6.1 applies to lamps with light source modules. The spec lists the light source as "LED modules on PCB", which reasonably reads as light source modules. The spec does not confirm that these meet the regulatory definition, so confidence is moderate. The wording matches the clause.

Clause 3.6.2 requires a module identification code. It starts with "MD", followed by the approval marking without the circle, with extra symbols where non-identical modules are used, and is shown in the drawings. It applies if the LED modules are light source modules, as the spec suggests. The candidate preserves these conditions.

Clause 3.6.3 requires light source modules to bear the rated voltage or voltage range marking. It applies given the LED modules in the lamp. The spec gives no voltage value, but the clause does not need one to apply. The wording matches the clause.

Paragraph 6.6 says Annex 4 gives the measurement methods for light intensity. The product has a rear position lamp and a stop lamp, and both are UN R7 devices. The wording "rear lamp functions" is slightly broad, because the reversing lamp and retro-reflector are outside R7. The obligation still holds for the R7 functions.

Paragraph 7.1 says all photometric and colorimetric measurements are made under the conditions in 7.1.1 to 7.1.4. Those conditions depend on the type of light source and control gear. The spec only says "LED modules on PCB", so it does not show which sub-paragraph applies. The candidate refers to the 7.1.1–7.1.4 set as a whole, so it keeps that condition. It applies to the R7 rear position and stop lamp functions.

Paragraph 7.4 requires the voltage applied to the lamp to be noted in the Annex 2 communication form. The product has rear position and stop functions, which are in R7 scope. The spec gives no voltage value, but the obligation is not tied to one.
Paragraph 7.5 requires the limits of the apparent surface along the reference axis of a light-signalling device to be determined. The rear position and stop lamps are such devices.

Paragraph 8 requires red or white light inside the grid field and no sharp colour variation outside it. The candidate keeps that wording. It applies to the rear position and stop lamps, and the red-tinted lens is consistent with it.
Paragraph 9 requires conformity of production procedures to follow Agreement Schedule 1 plus the listed requirements. It applies to R7 lamps such as this rear lamp.
Paragraph 9.1 requires lamps to be manufactured to conform to the approved type, with compliance with paragraphs 6 and 8 verified. The candidate matches this.
Paragraph 9.1.1 requires the Annex 5 minimum conformity of production control requirements to be met. This applies to the product's production.
Paragraph 9.1.2 requires the Annex 6 minimum sampling requirements for an inspector to be met. This applies to the product's production.

Annex 2 item 9.1 of the R7 communication form requires the colour of light emitted to be stated (red/white). The product has rear position and stop lamp functions, which R7 covers. Its outer lens is red-tinted, so red is a reasonable entry for those lamps. The candidate presents this as a documentation obligation, and that matches the clause. One caveat is that the reversing lamp in the same housing emits white and falls outside R7, but the candidate's colour statement is about the R7 lamp functions.

The product combines rear position and stop lamps (R7 lamp types) in one housing, so it is a grouped or combined lamp. Clause 4.3.2.2 requires each lamp's identification symbol, series of amendments and arrow if needed. The reversing lamp falls under a different regulation, but the clause still applies to the R7 functions.

Clause 4.3.2.2.1 allows marking on the appropriate light-emitting surface as one of two alternatives. The candidate keeps this as a permitted option and does not state that it is mandatory. It applies to the product's R7 lamps.
The product groups several lamps in one housing. If the group-marking alternative is used, clause 4.3.2.2.2 requires each grouped lamp to be clearly identified. The candidate keeps this condition.

Clause 4.3.2.3 applies when a single approval mark is used for combined lamps. The product is a combined lamp, so this is plausible. The candidate wording keeps the 'single approval mark' condition and the minimum-size rule. The spec does not say whether a single mark is actually used.

Clause 4.3.2.4 requires an approval number for each approved type of grouped or combined lamps and bars reuse of the number for another type. The product is a combined lamp type, so this applies. The candidate wording matches the clause.

Clause 4.3.4 requires the approval marking to be legible, indelible and visible when the device is fitted or when a movable part is opened. This applies to the product's R7-approved lamps. The candidate leaves out the placement permission, which does not change the obligation.

Section 5 applies the general and individual specifications of R48, R53, R74 or R86 to the lamp. They apply by vehicle category and only where verification at type approval is feasible. The product is an M1 lamp. The candidate keeps these conditions.
Clause 5.1 requires each supplied device to conform to paragraphs 6 and 8. The product is a supplied rear lamp device with rear position and stop functions covered by R7.

Annex 6 paragraph 5 says approval is withdrawn according to paragraph 10. Paragraph 4.2 sets the trigger: conformity is contested if at least one specimen deviates by more than 20 per cent, and the approval is then withdrawn. Paragraph 10 is titled "Penalties for non-conformity of production". The product's rear position lamp and stop lamp fall under UN R7 under definitions 1.2 and 1.3. The candidate takes the 20 per cent condition from 4.2, not from clause 5, but that fits the Annex 6 context. The reversing lamp and retro-reflector are not R7 items, but the candidate does not claim they are.

results.reason: The product combines rear position, stop and reversing lamps and a retro-reflector in one housing. That fits the grouped or combined assembly in Annex 3/8. The clause only gives marking examples, and the candidate correctly words the simplified marking as permissive ("may").
Annex 4/1.1 requires stray reflections to be avoided by masking during photometric measurements. The product has R7 lamps (rear position and stop), so this applies.
Annex 4/1.2 sets conditions for measurements whose results are challenged. The candidate keeps that condition and refers to items 1.2.1 to 1.2.3. The product's rear position lamp is covered by R7.

Annex 4/1.2.1 requires the measurement distance to satisfy the inverse-square law when results are challenged. The product's stop lamp is covered by R7, and the candidate keeps the challenge condition.

Annex 4/1.2.2 sets a receiver angular aperture of 10 arcminutes to 1 degree, applied when results are challenged. The candidate wording matches it. The cited product evidence (reversing illumination) is weak because R7 does not cover reversing lamps. The obligation still applies to the product's R7 position and stop lamp measurements.

Annex 4/1.2.3 deems an intensity requirement met if it is met within 1/4 degree of the direction of observation, applied when results are challenged. This applies to the product's R7 rear position lamp.

Annex 5 1.2 applies to the rear position and stop lamp functions of this M1 rear lamp. The source clause ends in a colon and continues into 1.2.1, which sets the 20% tolerance. The candidate's wording "are met" is a loose completion of that lead-in. Clause 205 supplies the tolerance.
Annex 5 1.2.1 sets a 20% limit on unfavourable deviation of measured values. It applies to the rear position and stop lamp functions in the product.
Annex 5 1.3 requires the paragraph 8 colorimetric requirements to be met in conformity checks. The product has a red rear position lamp and stop lamp behind a red-tinted lens.
Annex 5 2 requires the approval mark holder to carry out minimum verification tests for each lamp type at appropriate intervals. The product's rear position and stop lamps fall under R7.
Annex 5 2.1 says conformity tests cover photometric and colorimetric characteristics. This applies to the R7 lamp functions in the product.
Annex 5 2.2.1 says tests are generally carried out by the methods set out in the Regulation. This applies to the product's R7 lamp functions.
Annex 5 2.2.2 allows equivalent methods in manufacturer conformity tests with the competent authority's consent. The manufacturer must prove equivalence. The candidate keeps both conditions.

The product has rear position and stop lamp functions, which R7 covers. Annex 5 2.2.3 requires regular calibration of test apparatus and correlation with the competent authority's measurements when 2.2.1 and 2.2.2 are applied. The candidate adds the words 'photometric and chromaticity' to those methods, which is a minor embellishment.

The product has a stop lamp, which R7 covers. Annex 5 2.2.4 says the reference methods are always those of the Regulation, particularly for administrative verification and sampling. The candidate matches this.
Annex 5 2.3 requires lamps to be sampled at random from a uniform batch of the same type. The product is a series-produced rear lamp with R7 position and stop functions, so this applies.

Annex 5 2.4 requires photometric measurement of the sampled lamp for minimum values at the Annex 4 points and for the required chromaticity coordinates. The product's rear position and stop functions fall under R7, so this applies. The candidate matches the clause.

Annex 5 2.5 makes the manufacturer responsible for a statistical study and for defining acceptability criteria in agreement with the competent authority. The criteria must give a 95% confidence level that the minimum probability of passing an Annex 6 first-sampling spot check is 0.95. The candidate preserves these conditions, and the product's rear position lamp falls under R7.

Annex 6 1.1 treats mechanical and geometric conformity as satisfied if differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations. It applies to the product's R7 lamp functions. The candidate matches the clause.

Annex 6 1.2 says conformity of mass-produced lamps is not contested if the photometric performance of any lamp chosen at random meets Paragraph 6 when tested per Paragraph 7. The candidate paraphrases this. It leaves out the sub-conditions in 1.2.1 to 1.2.3, which the clause text only introduces, but it does not contradict them. The clause applies to the product's position and stop lamp functions.
